title.zh: 卷三百五十三 列傳第一百十二 何㮚 孫傅 陳過庭 張叔夜 聶昌 張閣 張近 鄭僅 宇文昌齡子:常 許幾 程之邵 龔原 崔公度 蒲卣
title.en: Volume 353 Biographies 112: He Li, Sun Fu, Chen Guoting, Zhang Shuye, Nie Chang, Zhang Ge, Zhang Jin, Zheng Jin, Yu Wenchangling and son: Chang, Xu Ji, Cheng Zhi Shao, Gong Yuan, Cui Gongdu, Pu You
title.raw: 卷三百五十三 列傳第一百十二 何㮚 孫傅 陳過庭 張叔夜 聶昌 張閣 張近 鄭僅 宇文昌齡子:常 許幾 程之邵 龔原 崔公度 蒲卣 Volume 353 Biographies 112: He Li, Sun Fu, Chen Guoting, Zhang Shuye, Nie Chang, Zhang Ge, Zhang Jin, Zheng Jin, Yu Wenchangling and son: Chang, Xu Ji, Cheng Zhi Shao, Gong Yuan, Cui Gongdu, Pu You

sentences.zh: 何㮚 孫傅 陳過庭 張叔夜 聶昌 張閣 張近 鄭僅 宇文昌齡子:常 許幾 程之邵 龔原 崔公度 蒲卣

translations.literal: He Li, Sun Fu, Chen Guoting, Zhang Shuye, Nie Chang, Zhang Ge, Zhang Jin, Zheng Jin, Yu Wenchangling and son Chang, Xu Ji, Cheng Zhi Shao, Gong Yuan, Cui Gongdu, Pu You
translations.idiomatic: He Li, Sun Fu, Chen Guoting, Zhang Shuye, Nie Chang, Zhang Ge, Zhang Jin, Zheng Jin, Yu Wenchangling and son Chang, Xu Ji, Cheng Zhi Shao, Gong Yuan, Cui Gongdu, and Pu You

sentences.zh: 何㮚，字文緽，仙井人。

translations.literal: He Li, styled Wenzhen, was a native of Xianjing.
translations.idiomatic: He Li, whose courtesy name was Wenzhen, came from Xianjing.

sentences.zh: 政和五年進士第一，擢秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenghe he placed first in the jinshi examination and was appointed proofreader in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He topped the jinshi lists in the fifth year of the Zhenghe reign and was raised to proofreader in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 逾年，提舉京畿學事，召為主客員外郎、起居舍人，遷中書舍人兼侍講。

translations.literal: After a year he was put in charge of educational affairs in the capital region, summoned as vice director of the Bureau of Receptions and recorder of imperial audiences, and promoted to drafting secretary and concurrent lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was charged with schools in the capital circuit, then recalled as vice director of the Bureau of Receptions and recorder of imperial audiences, and soon promoted to drafting secretary with a concurrent lectureship at court.

sentences.zh: 徽宗數從咨訪，欲付以言責。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong repeatedly sought his counsel and wished to entrust him with the duty of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong often consulted him and intended to give him the role of court remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 或論㮚與蘇軾鄉党，宗其曲學，出知遂寧府。

translations.literal: Some argued that Li was a fellow townsman of Su Shi and followed his heterodox learning, and he was sent out to serve as prefect of Suining.
translations.idiomatic: Critics claimed he was Su Shi's countryman and a follower of Su's unorthodox scholarship, so he was posted out as prefect of Suining.

sentences.zh: 已而留為御史中丞，論王黼奸邪專橫十五罪，黼既抗章請去，而尤豫未決。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was retained as censor-in-chief and charged Wang Fu with fifteen crimes of treachery, wickedness, and domineering conduct; Fu had already submitted a memorial asking to retire, yet the emperor still hesitated.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon kept on as censor-in-chief and impeached Wang Fu on fifteen counts of corruption and tyranny; though Fu had already asked to resign, the throne still wavered.

sentences.zh: 㮚繼上七章，黼及其党胡松年、胡益等皆罷，㮚亦以徽猷閣待制知泰州。

translations.literal: Li followed with seven more memorials; Fu and his partisans Hu Songnian, Hu Yi, and others were all dismissed, and Li was also made prefect of Taizhou with the title of Hanlin academician-at-large of the Huixiu Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Li sent seven further memorials until Fu and his allies Hu Songnian and Hu Yi were removed; Li himself was then made prefect of Taizhou as a Huixiu Pavilion academician-at-large.

sentences.zh: 欽宗立，復以中丞召。

translations.literal: When Emperor Qinzong acceded, Li was again summoned as censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: After Qinzong took the throne, Li was recalled as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 閱月，為翰林學士，進尚書右丞、中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Within a month he became a Hanlin academician and advanced to vice director of the right department of the Ministry of State and vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he entered the Hanlin Academy and rose to vice director of the right department and vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 會王雲使金帥斡離不軍還，言金人怒割三鎮緩，卻禮幣弗納曰，兼旬使不至，則再舉兵。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Yun returned from an embassy to the Jin commander Wanyan Woliba's army, reporting that the Jurchens were angry the cession of the three circuits was delayed, refused the tribute gifts, and said that if envoys did not arrive within ten days they would raise troops again.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun had just returned from Wanyan Woliba's camp with word that the Jurchens were furious at the delay in ceding the three frontier circuits, had rejected the tribute, and threatened to march again unless envoys came within ten days.

sentences.zh: 於是百官議從其請。

translations.literal: Thereupon the officials debated yielding to their demand.
translations.idiomatic: The court then debated acceding to the demand.

sentences.zh: 㮚曰：「三鎮，國之根本，奈何一旦棄之。

translations.literal: Li said, "The three circuits are the foundation of the state—how can we abandon them in a single stroke?
translations.idiomatic: Li said, "The three circuits are the nation's foundation—how can we cast them away at once?

sentences.zh: 況金人變詐罔測，安能保必信？

translations.literal: Moreover the Jurchens are treacherous and unpredictable—how can we be sure they will keep faith?
translations.idiomatic: And the Jurchens are treacherous and unpredictable—who can guarantee they will keep their word?

sentences.zh: 割亦來，不割亦來。」

translations.literal: If we cede they will come; if we do not cede they will come likewise."
translations.idiomatic: They will attack whether we cede the territory or not."

sentences.zh: 宰相主割議，㮚論辨不已，曰：「河北之民，皆吾赤子。

translations.literal: The chief ministers favored cession; Li argued without cease and said, "The people of Hebei are all our own children.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers favored cession, but Li kept arguing: "The people of Hebei are all our own children.

sentences.zh: 棄地則並其民棄之，豈為父母意哉？」

translations.literal: To abandon the land is to abandon the people with it—is that the mind of parents?"
translations.idiomatic: To surrender the land is to abandon the people with it—is that what parents do?"

sentences.zh: 帝頗悟。

translations.literal: The emperor was somewhat persuaded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was somewhat moved.

sentences.zh: 㮚請建四道總管，使統兵入援，以胡直孺、王襄、趙野、張叔夜領之。

translations.literal: Li requested the establishment of four regional commanders to lead troops in relief, with Hu Zhiru, Wang Xiang, Zhao Ye, and Zhang Shuye placed in charge.
translations.idiomatic: Li proposed four regional commanders to lead relief armies, appointing Hu Zhiru, Wang Xiang, Zhao Ye, and Zhang Shuye to the posts.

sentences.zh: 兵既回應，而唐恪、耿南仲、聶昌信和議，相與謀曰：「方繼好息民而調發不已，使金人聞之，奈何？」

translations.literal: The troops had already begun to respond when Tang Ke, Geng Nanzhong, and Nie Chang, who trusted in peace talks, consulted together and said, "We are just renewing friendship and resting the people, yet levies and mobilizations go on without end—if the Jurchens hear of this, what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Troops were already moving when Tang Ke, Geng Nanzhong, and Nie Chang, believers in peace, plotted together: "We are trying to restore amity and give the people rest, yet mobilizations never stop—what if the Jurchens hear of it?"

sentences.zh: 亟檄止之。

translations.literal: They urgently issued orders to halt them.
translations.idiomatic: They hurriedly ordered the mobilizations stopped.

sentences.zh: 㮚解政事，俄以資政殿大學士領開封尹。

translations.literal: Li left the administration and soon afterward served as academician of the Zizheng Hall and prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Li left the chief council and was soon made Zizheng Hall academician and prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 金兵長驅傅城下，帝罷恪相，而拜㮚為尚書右僕射兼中書侍郎，始復三省舊制。

translations.literal: Jin troops drove straight to the walls; the emperor dismissed Ke as chief minister and appointed Li right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and vice director of the Secretariat, restoring the old three-department system.
translations.idiomatic: As Jin armies swept to the capital, the emperor removed Tang Ke and made Li right grand councilor and vice director of the Secretariat, reviving the old three-department order.

sentences.zh: 時康王在河北，信使不通，㮚建議請以為元帥，密草詔稿上之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Kang was then in Hebei and couriers could not get through; Li proposed making him commander-in-chief and secretly drafted an edict for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: With the Prince of Kang in Hebei and communications cut, Li urged appointing him supreme commander and secretly drafted an edict for the throne.

sentences.zh: 乃以康王充天下兵馬大元帥，陳遘充兵馬元帥，宗澤、汪伯彥充副元帥。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Prince of Kang was made grand marshal of all armies, Chen Sui marshal, and Zong Ze and Wang Boyan deputy marshals.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Kang was named grand marshal of all forces, Chen Sui marshal, and Zong Ze and Wang Boyan his deputies.

sentences.zh: 京城失守，從幸金帥營，遂留不返。

translations.literal: When the capital fell he accompanied the emperor to the Jin commander's camp and was detained there.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell he followed the emperor to the Jin camp and never returned.

sentences.zh: 既而議立異姓，金人曰：「唯何㮚、李若水毋得預議。」

translations.literal: When they later debated enthroning someone of another surname, the Jurchens said, "Only He Li and Li Ruoshui may not take part in the deliberations."
translations.idiomatic: When enthroning a non-Song ruler was discussed, the Jurchens ruled that He Li and Li Ruoshui alone must be excluded."

sentences.zh: 既陷朔庭，㮚仰天大慟，不食而死，年三十九。

translations.literal: After falling into the northern court's hands, Li wailed to heaven and starved himself to death at the age of thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Once captive in the north, he cried to heaven and died by fasting at thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，詔以為觀文殿大學士、提舉玉局觀使，祿其家。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyan reign an edict made him academician of the Guanwen Hall and commissioner of the Jade Bureau, with stipends for his family.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianyan he was posthumously named Guanwen Hall academician and commissioner of the Jade Bureau, with stipends for his household.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，贈開府儀同三司，議者指其誤國，不行。

translations.literal: When word of his death arrived, posthumous elevation to Defender-in-Chief with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies was proposed, but critics charged he had harmed the state and it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: On news of his death a posthumous rank as Defender-in-Chief was proposed, but critics blamed him for the national disaster and it was denied.

sentences.zh: 秦檜自北還，具道其死時狀，乃改贈大學士，官其家七人。

translations.literal: When Qin Hui returned from the north he gave a full account of Li's death, whereupon the posthumous title was changed to grand academician and seven members of his family were given office.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui, back from the north, described how Li had died, and the court then granted him the posthumous title of grand academician and offices to seven kin.

sentences.zh: 孫傅，字伯野，海州人。

translations.literal: Sun Fu, styled Boye, was a native of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fu, courtesy name Boye, came from Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，中詞學兼茂科，為秘書省正字、校書郎、監察御史、禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and the special "Erudite Learning and Abundant Talent" examination, and served as collator in the Secretariat, proofreader, investigating censor, and vice director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi degree and the Erudite Learning and Abundant Talent examination, then served as collator, proofreader, investigating censor, and vice director of rites.

sentences.zh: 時蔡翛為尚書，傅為言天下事，勸其亟有所建，不然必敗。

translations.literal: When Cai Xiao was director of a ministry, Fu spoke to him of affairs under heaven and urged him to act quickly or he would surely fail.
translations.idiomatic: While Cai Xiao headed a ministry, Fu warned him about the state of the realm and urged swift action or ruin would follow.

sentences.zh: 翛不能用。

translations.literal: Xiao could not employ his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書少監，至中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and reached the post of drafting secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice director of the Secretariat and eventually to drafting secretary.

sentences.zh: 宣和末，高麗入貢，使者所過，調夫治舟，騷然煩費。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xuanhe reign Goryeo sent tribute; along the envoys' route corvée labor was levied to repair boats, causing uproar and heavy expense.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Xuanhe, Goryeo's tribute mission forced corvée labor and boat repairs along its route, stirring unrest and heavy costs.

sentences.zh: 傅言：「索民力以妨農功，而於中國無絲毫之益。」

translations.literal: Fu said, "To demand the people's strength and hinder farming brings China not the slightest benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Fu argued, "Drafting the people and disrupting the harvest brings the empire no benefit whatsoever."

sentences.zh: 宰相謂其所論同蘇軾，奏貶蘄州安置。

translations.literal: The chief minister said his argument matched Su Shi's and memorialized to banish him to Qizhou under restricted residence.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister claimed his views echoed Su Shi's and had him exiled to Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 給事中許翰以為傅論議雖偶與軾合，意亦亡他，以職論事而責之過矣，翰亦罷去。

translations.literal: The drafting reviewer Xu Han held that although Fu's argument happened to agree with Su Shi, his intent was otherwise blameless and to punish a man for doing his duty in remonstrance was excessive; Han was also dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Han argued that Fu's views merely coincided with Su Shi's and that punishing an official for speaking his office was unjust; Xu too was removed.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，召為給事中，進兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang he was summoned as drafting reviewer and promoted to minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingkang he was recalled as drafting reviewer and made minister of war.

sentences.zh: 上章乞復祖宗法度，欽宗問之，傅曰：「祖宗法惠民，熙、豐法惠國，崇、觀法惠奸。」

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial asking to restore the ancestral statutes; Qinzong questioned him, and Fu said, "The ancestral laws benefit the people; the Xining and Yuanfeng laws benefit the state; the Chongning and Zhenghe laws benefit villains."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to restore ancestral law; when Qinzong asked, Fu replied, "Ancestral law benefits the people; Xining and Yuanfeng law benefits the state; Chongning and Zhenghe law benefits villains."

sentences.zh: 時謂名言。

translations.literal: It was then called a famous saying.
translations.idiomatic: Men called it a classic line.

sentences.zh: 十一月，拜尚書右丞，俄改同知樞密院。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was appointed right vice director of the Ministry of State and soon changed to associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he became right vice director of state and soon associate commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 金人圍都城，傅日夜親當矢石。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens besieged the capital Fu personally faced arrows and stones day and night.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege Fu spent day and night on the walls under fire.

sentences.zh: 讀丘浚《感事詩》，有「郭京楊適劉無忌」之語，于市人中訪得無忌，龍衛兵中得京。

translations.literal: Reading Qiu Jun's "Poem on Stirring Events," with the line "Guo Jing, Yang Shi, Liu Wuji," he found Wuji among the townspeople and Jing among the Dragon Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiu Jun's poem he read the names Guo Jing, Yang Shi, and Liu Wuji; he found Wuji in the markets and Jing among the Dragon Guards.

sentences.zh: 好事者言京能施六甲法，可以生擒二將而掃蕩無餘，其法用七千七百七十七人。

translations.literal: Busybodies said Jing could perform the Six Jia method, capture the two enemy generals alive, and sweep the foe away entirely; the method required seven thousand seven hundred seventy-seven men.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor-mongers claimed Jing's Six Jia magic could capture the Jin generals alive and annihilate the enemy; it required exactly 7,777 men.

sentences.zh: 朝廷深信不疑，命以官，賜金帛數萬，使自募兵，無問技藝能否，但擇其年命合六甲者。

translations.literal: The court believed this utterly, gave him an office, bestowed tens of thousands in gold and silk, and let him recruit troops himself, asking nothing of skill but only choosing men whose years and fates matched the Six Jia.
translations.idiomatic: The court believed him completely, gave him rank and lavish gifts, and let him recruit troops solely by Six Jia birth-dates, ignoring martial skill.

sentences.zh: 所得皆市井遊惰，旬日而足。

translations.literal: Those obtained were all idle street loungers, and within ten days the quota was filled.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered only idle townsmen and filled the quota within ten days.

sentences.zh: 有武臣欲為偏裨，京不許，曰：「君雖材勇，然明年正月當死，恐為吾累。」

translations.literal: A military officer wished to serve as a subordinate commander; Jing would not allow it and said, "Though you are talented and brave, you are fated to die next year in the first month—I fear you would be a burden to me."
translations.idiomatic: When a brave officer offered to serve under him, Jing refused: "You are skilled, but you will die next first month and would only burden me."

sentences.zh: 其誕妄類此。

translations.literal: His absurdities were all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His nonsense ran along these lines.

sentences.zh: 敵攻益急，京談笑自如，云：「擇日出兵三百，可致太平，直襲擊至陰山乃止。」

translations.literal: As the enemy pressed harder Jing talked and laughed as before, saying, "On the chosen day three hundred troops will go out and bring peace, striking straight through to the Yin Mountains before stopping."
translations.idiomatic: As the assault intensified Jing remained cheerful, promising that three hundred men on the chosen day would restore peace and drive the enemy back to the Yin Mountains."

sentences.zh: 傅與何㮚尤尊信，傾心待之。

translations.literal: Fu and He Li especially honored and trusted him, devoting themselves to his service.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and He Li trusted him above all others and gave him their full support.

sentences.zh: 或上書見傅曰：「自古未聞以此成功者。

translations.literal: Someone submitted a letter to Fu saying, "From antiquity there has been no hearing of success by such means.
translations.idiomatic: Someone wrote to Fu: "History records no victory won this way.

sentences.zh: 正或聽之，姑少信以兵，俟有尺寸功，乃稍進任。

translations.literal: Even if you heed him, for the moment give him only a little trust and a few troops; wait until he achieves some small success before advancing his appointment further.
translations.idiomatic: If you must listen, give him only a small force first and promote him only after some real success.

sentences.zh: 今委之太過，懼必為國家羞。」

translations.literal: Now you entrust him too far—I fear it will surely bring shame on the state."
translations.idiomatic: Entrusting him so fully will surely disgrace the nation."

sentences.zh: 傅怒曰：「京殆為時而生，敵中瑣微無不知者。

translations.literal: Fu angrily said, "Jing was surely born for this age; there is nothing trivial in the enemy camp that he does not know.
translations.idiomatic: Fu snapped, "Jing was born for this crisis—he knows every detail of the enemy camp.

sentences.zh: 幸君與傅言，若告他人，將坐沮師之罪。」

translations.literal: You are fortunate to speak with Fu; if you tell others you will be punished for discouraging the army."
translations.idiomatic: You are lucky to speak only to me—tell anyone else and you will be charged with undermining morale."

sentences.zh: 揖使出。

translations.literal: He bowed him out.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed the man out.

sentences.zh: 又有稱「六丁力士」、「天關大將」、「北斗神兵」者，大率皆效京所為，識者危之。

translations.literal: There were also those calling themselves "Six Ding Strongmen," "Heaven Gate Great Generals," and "Northern Dipper Divine Troops"—for the most part all imitating what Jing did—and the discerning were alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Others styled themselves Six Ding Strongmen, Heaven Gate Generals, or Northern Dipper Spirit Soldiers, all copying Jing's methods, and thoughtful men were deeply worried.

sentences.zh: 京曰：「非至危急，吾師不出。」

translations.literal: Jing said, "Unless the danger is utmost, my troops will not go out."
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "My army will not march until the crisis is extreme."

sentences.zh: 㮚數趣之，徙期再三，乃啟宣化門出，戒守陴者悉下城，無得竊覘。

translations.literal: Li repeatedly urged him; the date was postponed again and again, and finally the Xuanhua Gate was opened for the sortie. He ordered the wall defenders all down from the ramparts and forbade anyone to peek.
translations.idiomatic: Li pressed him repeatedly until, after many delays, the Xuanhua Gate opened; defenders were ordered off the walls and forbidden to watch.

sentences.zh: 京與張叔夜坐城樓上。

translations.literal: Jing and Zhang Shuye sat on the gate tower.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Zhang Shuye sat on the gate tower watching.

sentences.zh: 金兵分四翼噪而前，京兵敗退，墮于護龍河，填屍皆滿，城門急閉。

translations.literal: Jin troops advanced in four wings with a clamor; Jing's soldiers were defeated and fell back, tumbling into the Imperial Dragon Moat until corpses filled it, and the gate was shut in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Jin forces charged in four wings; Jing's men broke and fell into the moat until it was choked with bodies, and the gate slammed shut.

sentences.zh: 京遽白叔夜曰：「須自下作法。」

translations.literal: Jing hurriedly told Shuye, "The spell must be cast from below."
translations.idiomatic: Jing told Shuye at once, "I must perform the rite from ground level."

sentences.zh: 因下城，引余眾南遁。

translations.literal: He then came down from the wall and led the remainder south in flight.
translations.idiomatic: He descended and fled south with the survivors.

sentences.zh: 是日，金人遂登城。

translations.literal: That day the Jurchens mounted the walls.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Jurchens took the walls.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，欽宗詣金帥營，以傅輔太子留守，仍兼少傅。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year Qinzong went to the Jin commander's camp; Fu was left to assist the crown prince in holding the capital, still serving concurrently as junior tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year two Qinzong went to the Jin camp, leaving Fu to assist the crown prince as regent and junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 帝兼旬不返，傅屢貽書請之。

translations.literal: The emperor did not return for more than ten days; Fu repeatedly sent letters asking him back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was gone more than ten days; Fu wrote again and again begging his return.

sentences.zh: 及廢立檄至，傅大慟曰：「吾惟知吾君可帝中國爾，苟立異姓，吾當死之。」

translations.literal: When the edict on deposition and enthronement arrived, Fu wailed greatly and said, "I know only that my lord can rule China; if another surname is enthroned I shall die for it."
translations.idiomatic: When the deposition edict came, Fu wept: "Only my sovereign can rule China; enthroning another house means my death."

sentences.zh: 金人來索太上、帝后、諸王、妃主，傅留太子不遣。

translations.literal: The Jurchens came demanding the retired emperor, empress, princes, and consorts; Fu kept the crown prince and would not send him.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens demanded the retired emperor, empress, princes, and consorts; Fu refused to surrender the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 密謀匿之民間，別求狀類宦者二人殺之，並斬十數死囚，持首送之，紿金人曰：「宦者欲竊太子出，都人爭鬥殺之，誤傷太子。

translations.literal: He secretly plotted to hide the prince among the people, separately sought out two men resembling eunuchs and killed them, and also beheaded more than ten condemned prisoners, sending their heads to deceive the Jurchens with the story, "Eunuchs tried to steal the prince away; the capital's people fought and killed them, mistakenly wounding the prince.
translations.idiomatic: He plotted to hide the prince among civilians, killed two men who looked like eunuchs and a dozen condemned prisoners, sent their heads north, and lied that eunuchs had tried to steal the prince and been killed in the riot, accidentally wounding him.

sentences.zh: 因帥兵討定，斬其為亂者以獻。

translations.literal: He then led troops to pacify the disturbance and beheaded those who had caused the riot as an offering.
translations.idiomatic: He then led troops to 'pacify' the riot and presented the heads of the supposed ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 苟不已，則以死繼之。」

translations.literal: If they did not stop, he would follow with his own death."
translations.idiomatic: If they persisted, he would die next."

sentences.zh: 越五日，無肯承其事者。

translations.literal: After five days no one would undertake the task.
translations.idiomatic: After five days no one would carry out the deception.

sentences.zh: 傅曰：「吾為太子傅，當同生死。

translations.literal: Fu said, "I am the crown prince's tutor and should share life and death with him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu said, "As the crown prince's tutor I must live or die with him.

sentences.zh: 金人雖不吾索，吾當與之俱行，求見二酋面責之，庶或萬一可濟。」

translations.literal: Though the Jurchens do not demand me, I shall go with him, seek audience with the two chieftains to reproach them to their faces, and perhaps in one case in ten thousand it may succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Even if they do not demand me, I will go with him, confront the two Jin commanders face to face, and perhaps—one chance in ten thousand—save him."

sentences.zh: 傅寓直皇城司，其子來省，叱之曰：「使汝勿來，而竟來邪！

translations.literal: Fu was on duty at the Imperial City Office; his son came to visit and he rebuked him, saying, "I told you not to come—yet you have come after all!
translations.idiomatic: Lodged at the Imperial City Office, he scolded his visiting son: "I told you not to come—yet here you are!

sentences.zh: 吾已分死國，雖汝百輩來何益！」

translations.literal: I have already resolved to die for the state—even if a hundred of you came what good would it do!"
translations.idiomatic: I have already given my life to the state—a hundred sons could not change that!"

sentences.zh: 揮使速去。

translations.literal: He waved him to leave at once.
translations.idiomatic: He waved him away.

sentences.zh: 子亦泣曰：「大人以身徇國，兒尚何言。」

translations.literal: The son also wept and said, "Father gives his body for the state—what more can your son say?"
translations.idiomatic: The son wept: "Father sacrifices himself for the realm—what can a son say?"

sentences.zh: 遂以留守事付王時雍而從太子出。

translations.literal: He then entrusted the regency to Wang Shiyong and followed the crown prince out.
translations.idiomatic: He handed the regency to Wang Shiyong and went out with the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 至南薰門，範瓊力止之，金守門者曰：「所欲得太子，留守何預？」

translations.literal: At the Nanxun Gate Fan Qiong tried hard to stop him; the Jin gate guards said, "What we want is the crown prince—what has the regent to do with it?"
translations.idiomatic: At Nanxun Gate Fan Qiong tried to hold him back; the Jin guards said, "We want only the crown prince—what business is the regent's?"

sentences.zh: 傅曰：「我宋之大臣，且太子傅也，當死從。」

translations.literal: Fu said, "I am a great minister of Song and the crown prince's tutor—I should die following him."
translations.idiomatic: Fu replied, "I am a Song minister and the crown prince's tutor; I must follow him even unto death."

sentences.zh: 是夕，宿門下，明日，金人召之去。

translations.literal: That evening he lodged beneath the gate; the next day the Jurchens summoned him away.
translations.idiomatic: That night he slept at the gate; the next day the Jurchens took him away.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，死於朔廷。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year he died in the northern court.
translations.idiomatic: The following second month he died in the north.

sentences.zh: 紹興中，贈開府儀同三司，諡曰忠定。

translations.literal: During the Shaoxing reign he was posthumously made Defender-in-Chief with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, with the posthumous title Zhongding.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shaoxing he was posthumously made Defender-in-Chief with Three Excellencies honors and given the posthumous name Loyal and Steadfast.

sentences.zh: 陳過庭

translations.literal: Chen Guoting
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guoting

sentences.zh: 陳過庭，字賓王，越州山陰人。

translations.literal: Chen Guoting, styled Binwang, was a native of Shanyin in Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guoting, courtesy name Binwang, came from Shanyin in Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 中進士第，為館陶主簿、澶州教授、知中牟縣，除國子博士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as registrar of Guantao, instructor at Dazhou, and magistrate of Zhongmou, then was appointed erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, served as Guantao registrar, Dazhou instructor, and Zhongmou magistrate, then became a National University erudite.

sentences.zh: 何執中、侯蒙器其才，薦之，擢祠部、吏部、右司員外郎。

translations.literal: He Zhizhong and Hou Meng valued his talent and recommended him; he was promoted to vice director in the Sacrificial and Personnel bureaus and in the right office of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhizhong and Hou Meng prized his talent and had him promoted to vice director in the sacrificial, personnel, and right secretariat offices.

sentences.zh: 使契丹，過庭初名揚庭，辭日，徽宗改賜今名。

translations.literal: On an embassy to the Khitan his original name was Yangting; on the day of his farewell audience Huizong changed and bestowed his present name.
translations.idiomatic: On a Khitan mission his name had been Yangting; at his farewell audience Huizong gave him his present name.

sentences.zh: 時人或傳契丹主苦風痹，又箭損一目，過庭歸證其妄，且勸帝以邊備為念。

translations.literal: Some at the time spread word that the Khitan ruler suffered from wind paralysis and had lost an eye to an arrow; on his return Guoting proved these tales false and urged the emperor to keep frontier defenses in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors claimed the Khitan ruler was crippled by palsy and blind in one eye; Guoting disproved them on his return and urged the emperor to strengthen frontier defenses.

sentences.zh: 適太常少卿、起居舍人。

translations.literal: He was then made vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and recorder of imperial audiences.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and recorder of imperial audiences.

sentences.zh: 宣和二年，進中書舍人；

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuanhe he was advanced to drafting secretary;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xuanhe he was promoted to drafting secretary;

sentences.zh: 才七日，遷禮部侍郎；

translations.literal: after only seven days he was transferred to vice minister of rites;
translations.idiomatic: seven days later to vice minister of rites;

sentences.zh: 未盡一月，又遷御史中丞兼侍讀。

translations.literal: before a month had passed he was again moved to censor-in-chief and concurrent lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: and within a month to censor-in-chief with a concurrent lectureship.

sentences.zh: 睦寇竊發，過庭言：「致寇者蔡京，養寇者王黼，竄二人，則寇自平。

translations.literal: When the Fang La bandits rose in rebellion Guoting said, "Cai Jing brought the bandits forth; Wang Fu nourished them—banish these two and the bandits will pacify themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When the Fang La rebellion broke out, Guoting said, "Cai Jing summoned these rebels and Wang Fu fed them—remove both and the rebellion will collapse.

sentences.zh: 又朱勔父子，本刑餘小人，交結權近，竊取名器，罪惡盈積，宜昭正典刑，以謝天下。」

translations.literal: Moreover Zhu Xun father and son were originally petty men from penal servitude who curried favor with the powerful, stole high titles, and piled up crimes—the proper penalties should be displayed openly to answer the realm."
translations.idiomatic: As for Zhu Xun and his son, penal outcasts who curried favor with the powerful and stole high office, their accumulated crimes demand public punishment to satisfy the realm."

sentences.zh: 由是大與權貴迕，翻陷以不舉劾之罪，罷知蘄州。

translations.literal: Thereby he greatly offended the powerful, who in turn trapped him with the charge of failing to impeach and had him dismissed to serve as prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: This put him at odds with the mighty, who turned on him with a charge of failing to impeach others and had him demoted to prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 未半道，責海州團練副使，黃州安置。

translations.literal: Before he had gone half the way he was demoted to deputy military training commissioner of Haizhou and placed under restricted residence at Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Halfway there he was demoted to deputy training commissioner of Haizhou and exiled to Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，得自便。

translations.literal: After three years he was allowed to go where he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he was free to move as he wished.

sentences.zh: 欽宗立，以集英殿修撰起知潭州；

translations.literal: When Qinzong acceded he was raised from compiler of the Jiying Hall to serve as prefect of Tanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: When Qinzong took the throne he was recalled from Jiying Hall compiler to prefect of Tanzhou;

sentences.zh: 未行，以兵部侍郎召，在道除中丞。

translations.literal: before he set out he was summoned as vice minister of war, and on the road was made censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: before he departed he was summoned as vice minister of war and made censor-in-chief en route.

sentences.zh: 初入見，帝諭以國家多難，每事當悉意盡言。

translations.literal: On his first audience the emperor instructed him that the state faced many hardships and that in every matter he should speak his mind fully.
translations.idiomatic: At his first audience the emperor told him the realm was in grave peril and urged him to speak freely on every issue.

sentences.zh: 於是節度使范訥丐歸環衛，過庭因言：「自崇寧以來，建旄鉞者多不由勳績，請除宗室及將帥立功者，餘並如訥例。」

translations.literal: Thereupon the military commissioner Fan Ne begged to return to the capital guard; Guoting took occasion to say, "Since Chongning, most who have received banners and axes have not earned them by merit—please remove all except imperial clansmen and generals who have won distinction in battle, and let the rest follow Ne's example."
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Ne asked to leave his command for a capital guard post, Guoting said, "Since Chongning most commanders have won their posts without merit—keep only imperial princes and generals with real victories, and let the rest follow Fan Ne home."

sentences.zh: 又乞辨宣仁後誣謗。

translations.literal: He also asked that the slanders against Empress Dowager Xuanren be cleared.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the calumnies against Empress Dowager Xuanren be refuted.

sentences.zh: 姚古擁兵不援太原，陳其可斬之罪七，竄諸嶺表。

translations.literal: Yao Gu held troops and did not relieve Taiyuan; Guoting set forth seven capital offenses warranting execution and had him banished beyond the mountain passes.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Gu had troops but refused to relieve Taiyuan; Guoting listed seven capital crimes against him and had him exiled to the far south.

sentences.zh: 進禮部尚書，擢右丞、中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He advanced to minister of rites and was promoted to right vice director and vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to minister of rites and was made right vice director and vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 議遣大臣割兩河與金，耿南仲以老、聶昌以親辭，過庭曰：「主憂臣辱，願效死。」

translations.literal: They debated sending a great minister to cede the two He provinces to the Jin; Geng Nanzhong declined on account of age and Nie Chang on account of kinship; Guoting said, "When the lord is troubled the minister is shamed—I wish to offer my life."
translations.idiomatic: The court debated sending a minister to cede the two He provinces; Geng Nanzhong pleaded age and Nie Chang family ties; Guoting said, "When the sovereign suffers, the minister is disgraced—I volunteer to go."

sentences.zh: 帝為揮涕歎息，固遣南仲、昌。

translations.literal: The emperor wiped away tears and sighed, but still sent Nanzhong and Chang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and sighed but still sent Nanzhong and Chang.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，過庭亦行，金人拘之軍中，因留不得還。

translations.literal: When the city fell Guoting went as well; the Jurchens detained him in their army and he was held and could not return.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell Guoting went too; the Jurchens held him in camp and never let him return.

sentences.zh: 建炎四年，卒于燕山，年六十，贈開府儀同三司，諡曰忠肅。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyan he died at Yanshan at the age of sixty; he was posthumously made Defender-in-Chief with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, with the posthumous title Zhongsu.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Yanshan in the fourth year of Jianyan, aged sixty, and was posthumously made Defender-in-Chief with the posthumous name Loyal and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 張叔夜

translations.literal: Zhang Shuye
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shuye

sentences.zh: 張叔夜，字嵇仲，侍中耆孫也。

translations.literal: Zhang Shuye, styled Jizhong, was a grandson of the palace attendant Zhang Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shuye, courtesy name Jizhong, was grandson of the palace attendant Zhang Qi.

sentences.zh: 少喜言兵，以蔭為蘭州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: In youth he delighted in discussing military affairs and entered office by yin privilege as recorder in Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved military talk and entered service by yin privilege as recorder in Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 州本漢金城郡，地最極邊，恃河為固，每歲河冰合，必嚴兵以備，士不釋甲者累月。

translations.literal: The prefecture was originally the Han commandery of Jincheng, the outermost frontier, relying on the river as its defense; each year when the river froze over troops had to stand on full alert and soldiers did not remove their armor for months.
translations.idiomatic: Lanzhou lay in the old Jincheng commandery on the farthest frontier, defended by the Yellow River; each winter when the ice formed, troops stood ready for months without doffing armor.

sentences.zh: 叔夜曰：「此非計也。

translations.literal: Shuye said, "This is no strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye said, "This is poor strategy.

sentences.zh: 不求要地守之，而使敵迫河，則吾既殆矣。」

translations.literal: If we do not seek and hold key ground but let the enemy press to the river, we are already in peril."
translations.idiomatic: If we fail to hold the vital ground and let the enemy reach the river, we are already lost."

sentences.zh: 有地曰大都者，介五路間，羌人入寇，必先至彼點集，然後議所向，每一至則五路皆竦。

translations.literal: There was a place called Dadu lying among the five circuits; when Qiang raiders invaded they always first gathered there to muster, then debated which way to go—each time they came all five circuits trembled.
translations.idiomatic: At Dadu, between the five circuits, Qiang raiders always mustered before choosing their route—each raid set all five circuits on edge.

sentences.zh: 叔夜按其形勢，畫攻取之策，訖得之，建為西安州，自是蘭無羌患。

translations.literal: Shuye studied its terrain, drew up a plan to attack and take it, and in the end captured it; it was established as Xi'an prefecture, and from then on Lanzhou had no Qiang trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye studied the terrain, planned its capture, took it, and established Xi'an prefecture there; Lanzhou was free of Qiang raids thereafter.

sentences.zh: 知襄城、陳留縣，蔣之奇薦之，易禮賓副使、通事舍人、知安肅軍，言者謂太優，還故官。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Xiangcheng and Chenliu; Jiang Zhiqi recommended him and he was changed to vice commissioner of ceremonial receptions, courier, and commander of Ansu Army; critics said the appointment was too generous and he was returned to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Xiangcheng and Chenliu he was recommended by Jiang Zhiqi for vice commissioner of receptions, courier, and Ansu Army command—critics called it too generous and he was restored to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 獻所為文，知舒、海、泰三州。

translations.literal: He presented his writings and was made prefect of Shu, Hai, and Tai prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He presented his writings and governed Shu, Hai, and Tai prefectures in turn.

sentences.zh: 大觀中，為庫部員外郎、開封少尹。

translations.literal: During the Daguan reign he was vice director in the Treasury Bureau and junior prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daguan he served as Treasury vice director and junior Kaifeng prefect.

sentences.zh: 復獻文，召試製誥，賜進士出身，遷右司員外郎。

translations.literal: He again presented writings, was summoned to an examination in drafting edicts, granted jinshi status, and promoted to vice director in the right office.
translations.idiomatic: He presented more writings, passed the edict-drafting examination, received jinshi status, and was made vice director of the right secretariat office.

sentences.zh: 使遼，宴射，首中的。

translations.literal: On an embassy to Liao, at a banquet archery contest he was the first to hit the target.
translations.idiomatic: On a Liao mission he won the banquet archery contest with the first shot.

sentences.zh: 遼人歎詫，求觀所引弓，以無故事，拒不與。

translations.literal: The Khitans marveled and asked to see the bow he had used; as there was no precedent he refused to show it.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitans marveled and asked to see his bow; with no precedent for such a request, he refused.

sentences.zh: 還，圖其山川、城郭、服器、儀範為五篇，上之。

translations.literal: On his return he illustrated their mountains and rivers, cities, dress and vessels, and ceremonial norms in five chapters and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Back home he submitted five illustrated reports on Liao terrain, cities, customs, and ritual.

sentences.zh: 從弟克公彈蔡京，京遷怒叔夜，摭司存微過，貶監西安草場。

translations.literal: His cousin Ke Gong impeached Cai Jing; Jing shifted his anger to Shuye, seized on a minor fault in his administration, and demoted him to oversee the Xi'an pasture.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Ke Gong impeached Cai Jing, who turned on Shuye, seized a minor administrative fault, and demoted him to oversee the Xi'an pasture.

sentences.zh: 久之，召為秘書少監，擢中書舍人、給事中。

translations.literal: After a long while he was summoned as vice director of the Secretariat and promoted to drafting secretary and drafting reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was recalled as vice director of the Secretariat and made drafting secretary and drafting reviewer.

sentences.zh: 時吏惰不虔，凡命令之出於門下者，預列銜，使書名而徐填其事，謂之：「空黃」。

translations.literal: At the time clerks were slack and irreverent; for every order issued from the Chancellery they pre-listed the signatures, had men write their names and slowly filled in the substance afterward—this was called "empty yellow."
translations.idiomatic: Clerks had grown slack: Chancellery orders were pre-signed with names filled in before the text was written—called "empty yellow" edicts.

sentences.zh: 叔夜極陳革其弊。

translations.literal: Shuye urgently set forth the need to reform this abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye urgently petitioned to end the abuse.

sentences.zh: 進禮部侍郎，又為京所忌，以徽猷閣待制再知海州。

translations.literal: He advanced to vice minister of rites but was again resented by Jing and was made Huixiu Pavilion academician-at-large and again prefect of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of rites, but Jing again resented him and sent him back to Haizhou as a Huixiu Pavilion academician-at-large.

sentences.zh: 宋江起河朔，轉略十郡，官軍莫敢嬰其鋒。

translations.literal: Song Jiang rose in Hebei and overran more than ten prefectures; government troops dared not meet his edge.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jiang rose in Hebei and swept through more than ten prefectures; government troops dared not face him.

sentences.zh: 聲言將至，叔夜使間者覘所向，賊徑趨海瀕，劫钜舟十餘，載鹵獲。

translations.literal: When word came that they were approaching, Shuye sent spies to watch their direction; the bandits went straight to the seashore, seized more than ten large ships, and loaded their plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing they were coming, Shuye sent scouts; the bandits raced to the coast, seized a dozen large ships, and loaded their loot.

sentences.zh: 於是募死士得千人，設伏近城，而出輕兵距海，誘之戰。

translations.literal: Thereupon he recruited a thousand dare-to-die troops, set ambushes near the city, and sent light forces to the coast to lure them into battle.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited a thousand volunteers, laid ambushes near the city, and sent light troops to the coast to draw them into battle.

sentences.zh: 先匿壯卒海旁，伺兵合，舉火焚其舟。

translations.literal: He first hid strong soldiers by the sea; when the armies joined he raised fires and burned their ships.
translations.idiomatic: He hid troops by the shore and, once battle joined, set fire to their fleet.

sentences.zh: 賊聞之，皆無鬥志，伏兵乘之，擒其副賊，江乃降。

translations.literal: When the bandits heard this they all lost fighting spirit; the ambush troops seized the moment, captured the deputy leader, and Jiang then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, the bandits lost heart; ambushers struck, captured the deputy leader, and Jiang surrendered.

sentences.zh: 加直學士，徙濟南府。

translations.literal: He was given the title of academician-at-large and transferred to Jinan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made academician-at-large and transferred to Jinan.

sentences.zh: 山東群盜猝至，叔夜度力不敵，謂僚吏曰：「若束手以俟援兵，民無噍類，當以計緩之。

translations.literal: Bandits in Shandong suddenly arrived; Shuye judged his strength insufficient and told his staff, "If we fold our hands waiting for reinforcements the people will be wiped out—we must use stratagem to delay them.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong bandits suddenly appeared; seeing he was outmatched, Shuye told his staff, "If we wait passively for reinforcements the people are doomed—we must stall them by guile.

sentences.zh: 使延三日，吾事濟矣。」

translations.literal: Gain me three days and my plan will succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Give me three days and I will prevail."

sentences.zh: 乃取舊赦賊文，俾郵卒傳至郡，盜聞，果小懈。

translations.literal: He then took an old amnesty for bandits and had couriers spread it through the prefecture; when the robbers heard they indeed slackened somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: He circulated an old bandit amnesty by courier; hearing it, the robbers hesitated.

sentences.zh: 叔夜會飲譙門，示以閒暇，遣吏諭以恩旨。

translations.literal: Shuye held a feast at the watchtower gate to show leisure and sent officials to announce the imperial grace.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted at the gate tower to show calm and sent officials to proclaim the amnesty.

sentences.zh: 盜狐疑相持，至暮未決。

translations.literal: The bandits wavered and held back, and by evening had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits wavered and by evening still had not moved.

sentences.zh: 叔夜發卒五千人，乘其惰擊之，盜奔潰，追斬數千級。

translations.literal: Shuye sent out five thousand troops, struck while they were slack, and the bandits fled in rout; pursuing them he cut down several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye sent five thousand men, struck while they hesitated, routed them, and slew thousands in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 以功進龍圖閣直學士、知青州。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to Longtu Pavilion academician-at-large and made prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For this victory he was made Longtu Pavilion academician-at-large and prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 靖康改元，金人南下，叔夜再上章乞假騎兵，與諸將並力斷其歸路，不報。

translations.literal: At the Jingkang reign change the Jurchens marched south; Shuye again memorialized asking to borrow cavalry and join the generals in cutting off their retreat—no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jingkang reign change the Jurchens marched south; Shuye again asked for cavalry to cut off their retreat with other generals—no answer came.

sentences.zh: 徙鄧州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 四道置帥，叔夜領南道都總管。

translations.literal: Four routes were given commanders; Shuye led the southern route as overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: Four regional commanders were appointed; Shuye led the southern route as overall commander.

sentences.zh: 金兵再至，欽宗手劄趣入衛。

translations.literal: When Jin troops came again Qinzong sent a personal letter urging him to enter and defend the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin returned, Qinzong wrote personally urging him to march to the capital's defense.

sentences.zh: 即自將中軍，子伯奮將前軍，仲熊將後軍，合三萬人，翌日上道。

translations.literal: He personally led the center army; his son Bofen led the vanguard and Zhongxiong the rear, thirty thousand in all, and set out the next day.
translations.idiomatic: He led the center himself, his son Bofen the vanguard and Zhongxiong the rear—thirty thousand men marching the next day.

sentences.zh: 至尉氏，與金遊兵遇，轉戰而前。

translations.literal: At Weishi he met Jin skirmishers and fought his way forward.
translations.idiomatic: At Weishi he fought through Jin skirmishers and pressed on.

sentences.zh: 十一月晦，至都，帝御南薰門見之，軍容甚整。

translations.literal: On the last day of the eleventh month he reached the capital; the emperor went to the Nanxun Gate to see him, and his troops were very orderly.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the eleventh month he reached the capital; the emperor met him at Nanxun Gate and found his troops perfectly disciplined.

sentences.zh: 入對，言賊鋒方銳，願如唐明皇之避祿山，暫詣襄陽以圖幸雍。

translations.literal: In audience he said the enemy's edge was still sharp and wished, as Tang Minghuang had fled An Lushan, to go temporarily to Xiangyang and plan a move to Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In audience he said the enemy was still strong and urged, as Tang Xuanzong had fled An Lushan, a temporary move to Xiangyang and then to Yong.

sentences.zh: 帝頷之。

translations.literal: The emperor nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded.

sentences.zh: 加延康殿學士。

translations.literal: He was made academician of the Yankang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Yankang Hall academician.

sentences.zh: 閏月，帝登城，叔夜陳兵玉津園，鎧甲光明，拜舞城下。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month the emperor ascended the wall; Shuye arrayed troops in the Yujin Garden, their armor bright, and bowed and danced below the wall.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month the emperor mounted the walls; Shuye paraded his men in Yujin Garden in gleaming armor and bowed below.

sentences.zh: 帝益喜，進資政殿學士，令以兵入城，俄簽書樞密院。

translations.literal: The emperor was still more pleased, advanced him to Zizheng Hall academician, ordered his troops into the city, and soon made him signing commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the emperor made him Zizheng Hall academician, brought his troops inside, and soon named him signing commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 連四日，與金人大戰，斬其金環貴將二人。

translations.literal: For four days straight he fought great battles with the Jurchens and beheaded two of their gold-ring noble generals.
translations.idiomatic: For four days he fought the Jurchens and slew two of their gold-ring commanders.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使齎蠟書，以褒寵叔夜之事檄告諸道，然迄無赴者。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys bearing sealed letters to proclaim Shuye's deeds and summon the circuits, yet in the end none came.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent sealed letters praising Shuye and summoning the circuits, but none came.

sentences.zh: 城陷，叔夜被創，猶父子力戰。

translations.literal: When the city fell Shuye was wounded but father and sons still fought with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he was wounded, yet he and his sons kept fighting.

sentences.zh: 車駕再出郊，叔夜因起居叩馬而諫，帝曰：「朕為生靈之故，不得不親往。」

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went out to the suburbs again Shuye, attending court, seized the horse's bridle to remonstrate; the emperor said, "For the sake of the living I must go in person."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went out to the suburbs again, Shuye seized the bridle and pleaded; the emperor said, "For the people's sake I must go myself."

sentences.zh: 叔夜號慟再拜，眾皆哭。

translations.literal: Shuye wailed and bowed twice; all wept.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye wailed and bowed twice, and all wept.

sentences.zh: 帝回首字之曰：「嵇仲努力！」

translations.literal: The emperor looked back and addressed him by his style: "Jizhong, do your utmost!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor looked back and called, "Jizhong, do your utmost!"

sentences.zh: 金人議立異姓，叔夜謂孫傅曰：「今日之事，有死而已。」

translations.literal: When the Jurchens debated enthroning someone of another surname Shuye said to Sun Fu, "In today's affair there is only death."
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens debated enthroning a non-Song ruler, Shuye told Sun Fu, "Today there is only death."

sentences.zh: 移書二帥，請立太子以從民望。

translations.literal: He sent letters to the two commanders asking that the crown prince be enthroned to satisfy the people's hope.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote both Jin commanders urging that the crown prince be enthroned to satisfy the people.

sentences.zh: 二帥怒，追赴軍中，至則抗請如初，遂從以北。

translations.literal: The two commanders were angry and had him pursued into their camp; when he arrived he pleaded as before and was taken north with them.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders were furious, seized him, and when he still pleaded as before took him north.

sentences.zh: 道中不食粟，唯時飲湯。

translations.literal: On the road he ate no grain, drinking only broth from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: On the march he ate no grain, drinking only broth.

sentences.zh: 既次白溝，馭者曰：「過界河矣。」

translations.literal: When they halted at the Bai Gou the driver said, "We have crossed the border river."
translations.idiomatic: At Bai Gou the driver said, "We have crossed the border river."

sentences.zh: 叔夜乃矍然起，仰天大呼，遂不復語。

translations.literal: Shuye started up in alarm, cried out to heaven, and spoke no more.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye started up, cried to heaven, and never spoke again.

sentences.zh: 明日，卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: The next day he died at the age of sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he died, aged sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，贈開府儀同三司，諡曰忠文。

translations.literal: When word of his death arrived he was posthumously made Defender-in-Chief with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, with the posthumous title Zhongwen.
translations.idiomatic: On news of his death he was posthumously made Defender-in-Chief with the posthumous name Loyal and Literary.

sentences.zh: 聶昌，字幸遠，撫州臨川人。

translations.literal: Nie Chang, styled Xingyuan, was a native of Linchuan in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Chang, courtesy name Xingyuan, came from Linchuan in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 始繇太學上舍釋褐，為相州教授。

translations.literal: He first left the upper dormitory of the Imperial University and entered office, serving as instructor in Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Imperial University's upper dormitory for office as instructor in Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 用蔡攸薦，召除秘書郎，擢右司員外郎。

translations.literal: Through Cai You's recommendation he was summoned and made secretary; he was promoted to vice director in the right office.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Cai You, he was made secretary and then vice director of the right secretariat office.

sentences.zh: 時三省大吏階官視卿監者，立都司上，昌以名分未正，極論之。

translations.literal: At the time great clerks of the three departments whose rank equaled that of masters of ceremonies were placed above the chief secretariat offices; Chang argued urgently that this inverted proper status.
translations.idiomatic: Senior clerks of the three departments were ranked above the chief secretariat offices; Chang protested that this inverted proper precedence.

sentences.zh: 詔自今至朝請大夫止。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that from now on this would apply only up to the rank of Grandee for Court Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: An edict limited the practice to ranks no higher than Grandee for Court Discussion.

sentences.zh: 以直龍圖閣為湖南轉運使，還為太府卿、戶部侍郎，改開封尹，復為戶部。

translations.literal: As Longtu Pavilion academician-at-large he was made transport commissioner for Hunan, then returned as director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and vice minister of revenue, changed to prefect of Kaifeng, and again made minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: As Longtu Pavilion academician he became Hunan transport commissioner, then treasury director and vice minister of revenue, then Kaifeng prefect, then minister of revenue again.

sentences.zh: 昌本厚王黼，既而從蔡京，為黼所中，罷知德安府。

translations.literal: Chang had been close to Wang Fu but later followed Cai Jing; Fu struck at him and he was dismissed to serve as prefect of De'an.
translations.idiomatic: Chang had been close to Wang Fu but later sided with Cai Jing; Fu struck back and he was demoted to prefect of De'an.

sentences.zh: 又以鄉人訟，謫崇信軍節度副使，安置衡州。

translations.literal: Because of a lawsuit by a fellow townsman he was demoted to deputy military commissioner of Chongxin Army and placed under restricted residence at Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A lawsuit by a fellow townsman brought demotion to deputy commissioner of Chongxin Army and exile to Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 欽宗立，吳敏用事，以昌猛厲徑行為可助己，自散地授顯謨閣直學士、知開德府，道拜兵部侍郎，進戶部尚書，領開封府。

translations.literal: When Qinzong acceded Wu Min was in power and thought Chang's fierce directness could help him; from exile he was made Xianmo Pavilion academician-at-large and prefect of Kaide, and on the road was made vice minister of war, advanced to minister of revenue, and put in charge of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinzong took the throne Wu Min, in power, valued Chang's fierce directness; from exile Chang was made Xianmo Pavilion academician and Kaide prefect, then vice minister of war en route, minister of revenue, and Kaifeng intendant.

sentences.zh: 昌遇事奮然不顧，敢誅殺。

translations.literal: Chang in affairs rushed forward without regard and dared to execute and kill.
translations.idiomatic: Chang acted boldly without hesitation and did not shrink from executions.

sentences.zh: 敏度不為用，始憚之，引唐恪、徐處仁共政，獨遺昌。

translations.literal: Min judged he could not be used, began to fear him, brought in Tang Ke and Xu Churen to share government, and left Chang out alone.
translations.idiomatic: Min found he could not control him, grew wary, brought Tang Ke and Xu Churen into government, and left Chang out.

sentences.zh: 李綱之罷，太學生陳東及士庶十余萬人，撾鼓伏闕下，經日不退，遇內侍輒殺之，府尹王時雍麾之不去。

translations.literal: When Li Gang was dismissed the National University student Chen Dong and more than a hundred thousand commoners beat drums and lay before the palace gate, not leaving for a whole day; whenever they met eunuchs they killed them, and the prefect Wang Shiyong waved them off but they would not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Gang was dismissed, student Chen Dong and more than a hundred thousand people drummed and knelt at the palace gate all day, killing eunuchs they met; prefect Wang Shiyong could not disperse them.

sentences.zh: 帝顧昌俾出諭旨，即相率聽命。

translations.literal: The emperor looked to Chang and had him go out to announce the imperial will; they then followed one another in obedience.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Chang out with the imperial message, and the crowd obeyed at once.

sentences.zh: 王時雍欲置東等獄，昌力言不可，乃止。

translations.literal: Wang Shiyong wished to imprison Dong and the others; Chang strongly said this could not be done, and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shiyong wanted to imprison Chen Dong and the others; Chang strongly opposed it and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 昌再尹京，惡少年怙亂，晝為盜，入官民家攘金帛；

translations.literal: When Chang again governed the capital, wicked youths relied on the disorder to rob by day, entering officials' and commoners' homes to seize gold and silk;
translations.idiomatic: When Chang again governed the capital, hoodlums exploited the chaos to rob by day, breaking into homes to seize gold and silk;

sentences.zh: 且去，輒自縛黨中三兩輩，聲言擒盜，持仗部走委巷，乃釋縛，分所掠而去。

translations.literal: and when they left they would bind two or three of their gang, proclaim they were capturing robbers, march with weapons through back alleys, then release the bonds and divide the plunder before departing.
translations.idiomatic: then bind a few accomplices, claim they were catching robbers, march through alleys with weapons, release them, and split the loot.

sentences.zh: 人不奠居。

translations.literal: People could not live in peace.
translations.idiomatic: No one could live in peace.

sentences.zh: 昌悉彈治正法，而縱博弈不之問，或謂令所禁，昌曰：「姑從所嗜，以懈其謀，是正所以禁其為非爾。」

translations.literal: Chang prosecuted all by the proper law, yet allowed gambling without inquiry; some said this was forbidden, and Chang said, "For the moment indulge their desires to slacken their plotting—that is precisely how to stop their wrongdoing."
translations.idiomatic: Chang prosecuted crime strictly but ignored gambling; when told it was forbidden, he said, "Let them indulge their vices to dull their schemes—that is how you stop their crimes."

sentences.zh: 昌舊名山，至是，帝謂其有周昌抗節之義，乃命之曰「昌」。

translations.literal: Chang's original name was Shan; at this time the emperor said he had the righteous integrity of Zhou Chang and therefore ordered him named "Chang."
translations.idiomatic: His name had been Shan; the emperor now said he had Zhou Chang's integrity and renamed him Chang.

sentences.zh: 京師復戒嚴，拜同知樞密院。

translations.literal: When the capital was again placed under martial law he was made associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was again placed under martial law he was made associate commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 入謝，即陳捍敵之策，曰：「三關四鎮，國家藩籬也，聞欲以畀敵，一朝渝盟，何以制之？

translations.literal: On entering to give thanks he at once set forth a plan to resist the enemy, saying, "The three passes and four garrisons are the state's screen; I hear they are to be given to the foe—if they break the treaty in a morning, how will we control them?
translations.idiomatic: In his thanks audience he urged resistance: "The three passes and four garrisons are our screen; if we give them away and the enemy breaks faith tomorrow, how will we restrain them?

sentences.zh: 願勿輕與，而檄天下兵集都畿，堅城守以遏其沖，簡禁旅以備出擊，壅河流以斷歸路。

translations.literal: I beg that they not be lightly surrendered, but that orders go out summoning troops from all under heaven to the capital region, holding the walls firm to check their thrust, selecting palace guards to prepare sorties, and damming the rivers to cut off their retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Do not surrender them lightly; summon troops to the capital, hold the walls, ready the palace guard to strike, and dam the rivers to cut off retreat.

sentences.zh: 前有堅城，後有大河，勁兵四面而至，彼或南下，墮吾網中矣。

translations.literal: With strong walls before and a great river behind, and crack troops arriving from all sides, if they march south they will fall into our net.
translations.idiomatic: With strong walls ahead, a great river behind, and crack troops converging from every side, if they march south they will fall into our net.

sentences.zh: 臣願激合勇義之士，設伏開關，出不意掃其營以報。」

translations.literal: Your servant wishes to rouse brave and righteous men, set ambushes and open the gates, and by surprise sweep their camp in reply."
translations.idiomatic: I would rouse the brave, set ambushes, open the gates, and surprise their camp in revenge."

sentences.zh: 帝壯之，命提舉守禦，得以便宜行事。

translations.literal: The emperor was heartened and ordered him to take charge of defense, with authority to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impressed and put him in charge of defense with discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 會金人再議和，割兩河，須大臣報聘。

translations.literal: It happened that the Jurchens again negotiated peace and the two He provinces were to be ceded; a great minister had to go on a return embassy.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens again negotiated peace, requiring cession of the two He provinces and a ministerial embassy.

sentences.zh: 詔耿南仲及昌往，昌言：「兩河之人忠議勇勁，萬一不從，必為所執，死不瞑目矣。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Geng Nanzhong and Chang to go; Chang said, "The people of the two He provinces are loyal, principled, brave, and fierce—if by any chance they do not obey, we will surely be seized by them and die with eyes unclosed.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Nanzhong and Chang were ordered to go; Chang said, "The people of the two He provinces are loyal and fierce—if they refuse, we will be seized and die in shame.

sentences.zh: 儻和議不遂，臣當分遣官屬，促勤王之師入衛。」

translations.literal: If by chance the peace talks fail, your servant will dispatch subordinates in separate groups to urge relief armies to enter and defend the capital.
translations.idiomatic: If peace fails, I will dispatch officials to urge relief armies to march to the capital's defense.

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: [The emperor] granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 行次永安，與金將黏罕遇，其從者稱閤門舍人，止昌徹傘，令用榜子贊名引見，昌不可，爭辨移時，卒以客禮見。

translations.literal: When the journey reached Yong'an, they met the Jin general Nianhan; his attendants called themselves Attendants of the Gatefold, stopped Chang from lowering his parasol, and ordered that his name be announced on a placard before introduction—Chang refused; they argued for a long time; in the end he was received with guest rites.
translations.idiomatic: En route at Yong'an they met the Jin general Nianhan. His escorts, claiming to be Gatefold attendants, made Chang close his parasol and insisted he be announced by name on a placard before audience. After prolonged argument he was at last received as a guest.

sentences.zh: 昌往河東，至絳，絳人閉壁拒之。

translations.literal: Chang went to Hedong; when he reached Jiang, the people of Jiang shut their walls and refused him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang proceeded to Hedong; at Jiang the townspeople barred their gates against him.

sentences.zh: 昌持詔抵城下，縋而登。

translations.literal: Chang held the imperial edict, came beneath the city wall, and was hauled up by rope.
translations.idiomatic: He brought the edict to the foot of the wall and was drawn up by rope.

sentences.zh: 州鈐轄趙子清麾眾害昌，抉其目而臠之，年四十九。

translations.literal: The prefectural commander Zhao Ziqing directed the crowd to harm Chang, gouged out his eyes and minced his flesh; he was forty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural commander Zhao Ziqing incited the mob to kill Chang—they gouged out his eyes and dismembered him. He was forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 建炎四年，始贈觀文殿大學士，諡曰忠湣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyan, he was posthumously endowed Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, with the posthumous title Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 4 (1130) he was posthumously made Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, with the posthumous title Zhongmin ("loyal and lamented").

sentences.zh: 父用之，年九十，以憂死。

translations.literal: His father Yongzhi, aged ninety, died from grief.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yongzhi, ninety years old, died of grief.

sentences.zh: 昌為人疏雋，喜周人之急，然恩怨太明，睚眥必報。

translations.literal: Chang as a man was open and talented, fond of relieving others' urgencies, yet gratitude and resentment were too clear—he would revenge the least slight.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was generous and quick to aid others in need, but he bore grudges sharply and repaid every slight.

sentences.zh: 王黼之死，昌實遣客刺之，棄屍道旁。

translations.literal: At Wang Fu's death, Chang had in fact sent a retainer to assassinate him and abandoned the corpse by the road.
translations.idiomatic: Chang had actually sent an agent to assassinate Wang Fu; the body was left by the roadside.

sentences.zh: 遂附耿南仲取顯位，左右其說以誤國，卒至禍變，而身亦不免焉。

translations.literal: He then attached himself to Geng Nanzhong to obtain prominent rank, swayed his counsels to mislead the state, and in the end when calamity came his person too could not escape.
translations.idiomatic: He then aligned with Geng Nanzhong for high office, abetted his policies to the nation's harm, and when disaster came could not escape himself.

sentences.zh: 張閣，字台卿，河陽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Ge, style Taizheng, was a native of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ge, courtesy name Taizheng, was from Heyang.

sentences.zh: 第進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 崇甯初，由衛尉主簿遷祠部員外郎；

translations.literal: In early Chongning, from Recorder of the Guard Chamber he was moved to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites;
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongning era he rose from Recorder of the Guard Chamber to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites;

sentences.zh: 資閱淺，為掌制者所議，蔡京主之，乃止。

translations.literal: his qualifications and experience were shallow; the drafters of edicts discussed this, but Cai Jing supported him and it stopped there.
translations.idiomatic: his résumé was thin and the edict drafters objected, but Cai Jing backed him and the matter ended.

sentences.zh: 俄徙吏部，遷宗正少卿、起居舍人，屬疾不能朝，改顯謨閣待制、提舉崇福宮。

translations.literal: Soon he moved to the Ministry of Personnel, was promoted Registrar of the Imperial Clan and Chamberlain for Attending the Emperor; when illness prevented court attendance, he was made Attendant Gentleman of the Xianmo Pavilion and put in charge of Chongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He soon transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, became Registrar of the Imperial Clan and Attending Scribe; when illness kept him from court he was made Attendant Gentleman of the Xianmo Pavilion and superintendent of Chongfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 疾愈，拜給事中、殿中監，為翰林學士。

translations.literal: When recovered, he was made Supervising Censor, Director of the Palace Bureau, and Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: After recovery he was appointed Supervising Censor and Director of the Palace Bureau, then Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 河北諸帥以繕城訖役，降獎詔，有中貴人為之地，將繼此策賞。

translations.literal: The commanders of Hebei, for completing city repairs, received rewarding edicts; a powerful eunuch spoke on their behalf and they were to continue this policy of rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei commanders who finished repairing fortifications received commendatory edicts; a palace eunuch interceded for them and similar rewards were to follow.

sentences.zh: 閣言：「此牧伯常職，若獎之，恐開邀功生事之路。」

translations.literal: Ge said: "This is the regular duty of regional governors; if rewarded, I fear it opens a path to inviting merit and stirring trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Ge argued: "Fortifying cities is a governor's ordinary duty; rewarding it would invite opportunism and border incidents."

sentences.zh: 徽宗曰：「卿言是也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong said: "Your words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: Huizong replied: "You are right."

sentences.zh: 格不下。

translations.literal: The edict was not issued.
translations.idiomatic: The reward edict was withheld.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜盛寒草制稿進，帝猶坐，賞其警敏，賜詩以為寵。

translations.literal: Once on a bitterly cold night he submitted a draft edict; the emperor was still seated, prized his alertness, and bestowed a poem as favor.
translations.idiomatic: One freezing night he presented a draft memorial while the emperor was still at his desk; Huizong praised his quickness and granted him an inscribed poem.

sentences.zh: 京免相，閣當制，歷數其過，詞語遒拔，人士多傳誦之。

translations.literal: When Jing was dismissed from chancellor, Ge drafted the edict, enumerating his faults—language forceful and elevated; gentlemen widely circulated and recited it.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing was removed as chief councilor, Ge wrote the dismissal edict listing his crimes in forceful prose that officials widely copied and recited.

sentences.zh: 京復相，以龍圖閣學士知杭州。

translations.literal: Jing returned as chancellor; Ge was made Hanlin Academician of the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing returned to power, Ge was made Academician of the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 浙部和買絹，杭獨居十三，戶有至數百匹者，閣請均之他郡。

translations.literal: Zhe circuits' coordinated silk purchase—Hangzhou alone bore thirteen parts; some households owed hundreds of bolts. Ge requested spreading it to other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhe's collective silk levy Hangzhou alone shouldered thirteen shares, with some households owing hundreds of bolts; Ge asked that the burden be shared with neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 杭久闕守，閣經理有敘，去惡少年之為人害者，州以理聞。

translations.literal: Hangzhou long lacked a prefect; Ge managed affairs in order, removed delinquent youths who harmed people; the prefecture reported good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Hangzhou had long been without a prefect; Ge put administration in order, cleared out troublemaking youths, and the circuit reported his effective rule.

sentences.zh: 召拜兵部尚書兼侍讀，復為學士，上日特賜敕詔，且有意大用，未幾，卒，年四十六。

translations.literal: Summoned as Minister of War and concurrent Lecturer, again Academician; on an audience day specially granted an edict of appointment, and there was intent to use him greatly—but soon he died, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Minister of War and imperial reader, again made Hanlin Academician; the emperor personally issued a promotion edict with intent to elevate him further, but he died soon after at forty-six.

sentences.zh: 閣初出守杭，思所以固寵，辭日，乞自領花石綱事，應奉由是滋熾雲。

translations.literal: When Ge first went out to guard Hangzhou, thinking how to secure favor, on his farewell audience he asked to take charge of the Flower and Stone Convoy himself—thus the supply service grew ever more extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: On first leaving for Hangzhou he sought to secure imperial favor and at his farewell audience asked to oversee the Flower-and-Stone Convoy himself—after which the tribute service grew vastly more oppressive.

sentences.zh: 張近，字幾仲，開封人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jin, style Jizhong, was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jin, courtesy name Jizhong, was from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 第進士，累遷大理正、發運使。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly promoted to Correcting Officer of the Court of Judicial Review and Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi graduate, he rose through posts including Correcting Officer of the Court of Judicial Review and Transport Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 呂溫卿以不法聞，近受詔鞫治，哲宗諭之曰：「此出朕命，卿毋畏惠卿。」

translations.literal: Lü Wenqing was known for lawlessness; Jin received an edict to investigate. Emperor Zhezong instructed him: "This proceeds from my command—do not fear Huiqing."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wenqing had a reputation for misconduct; Jin was ordered to investigate him. Zhezong told him: "This mission comes from me—do not fear Huiqing."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「法之所在，雖陛下不能使臣輕重，何惠卿也？」

translations.literal: He replied: "Where the law stands, even Your Majesty cannot make your servant bend severity or leniency—what of Huiqing?"
translations.idiomatic: Jin answered: "Where the law applies, even Your Majesty cannot make me bend it—why should I fear Huiqing?"

sentences.zh: 溫卿謾不肯置對，近言：「溫卿所坐明白，儻聽其蔓詞，懼為株連者累。」

translations.literal: Wenqing evasively refused to answer. Jin said: "Wenqing's offenses are clear; if we listen to his circuitous words, I fear those implicated in chains will suffer."
translations.idiomatic: Wenqing stonewalled the interrogation. Jin said: "His guilt is plain; if we indulge evasive testimony, others caught in the net will suffer."

sentences.zh: 詔以眾證定其罪。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his guilt fixed by the multitude of evidence.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered conviction on the weight of collective testimony.

sentences.zh: 提舉河北東路常平、西路刑獄，入為刑部員外郎、大理少卿，以集賢殿修撰知瀛州。

translations.literal: He was commissioner for Eastern Hebei Constant Granary and Western Circuit criminal prisons; entered as Vice Director of Justice and Vice President of Judicial Review; as Academician Editor of the Hall of Assembled Worthies he became prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised the Eastern Hebei granary and Western Hebei prisons, then entered the capital as Vice Director of Justice and Vice President of the Court of Judicial Review, and as Academician Editor governed Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 遼使為夏人請命，而宿兵以臨我，近請亦出秦甲戍北道，伐其謀。

translations.literal: A Liao envoy pleaded for the Xia people while encamped troops pressed us; Jin requested also sending Qin armor north by the western route to thwart their plot.
translations.idiomatic: A Liao envoy interceded for the Tanguts while Liao troops massed on the border; Jin proposed deploying Qin troops along the northern route to counter their scheme.

sentences.zh: 邊人呂懺兒入瓦橋為盜，吏執之，遼人因略宋民為質。

translations.literal: The border man Lü San'er entered Waqiao to rob; officials seized him; Liao men therefore seized Song civilians as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: A frontier man named Lü San'er crossed into Waqiao to plunder and was arrested; the Liao then abducted Song civilians as hostages.

sentences.zh: 近言：「朝廷方繼好息民，當使曲在彼。

translations.literal: Jin said: "The court is renewing amity and resting the people—wrong should be made to lie on their side.
translations.idiomatic: Jin urged: "The court seeks renewed peace and relief for the people—the fault should rest with them.

sentences.zh: 一偷之得失，不足為輕重，釋之便。」

translations.literal: The gain or loss of one thief is not enough to weigh heavily—releasing him is convenient.
translations.idiomatic: One thief is not worth a diplomatic crisis; release him.

sentences.zh: 滄民漁於海，遼卒利其饒，而私舉網取魚。

translations.literal: Cangzhou people fished at sea; Liao soldiers coveted their abundance and privately cast nets to take fish.
translations.idiomatic: Cangzhou fishermen worked offshore; Liao soldiers, coveting the catch, illegally cast nets in Song waters.

sentences.zh: 守兵與之鬥，斬級三十二，州將請賞之。

translations.literal: Garrison troops fought them and beheaded thirty-two; the prefectural commander requested rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison fought them and took thirty-two heads; the prefect requested battle honors.

sentences.zh: 或言所殺乃平人，宜論如律，議弗決。

translations.literal: Some said those killed were civilians and should be judged by law; deliberation did not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued the dead were civilians and the troops should be prosecuted; the court could not agree.

sentences.zh: 近言：「邊人貪利喜功，遂賞之，則為國起怨；

translations.literal: Jin said: "Border people are greedy for profit and fond of merit—if rewarded, the state will breed resentment;
translations.idiomatic: Jin warned: "Frontier troops are greedy and eager for glory—rewarding them will invite Liao resentment;

sentences.zh: 然彼挾兵涉吾地，謂之非盜可乎？

translations.literal: yet they carried arms across our land—can we call them not bandits?
translations.idiomatic: yet they crossed our territory armed—can we deny they were raiders?

sentences.zh: 如罪以擅興，他日將誰使禦敵？

translations.literal: If punished for unauthorized action, who later will be sent to resist the enemy?
translations.idiomatic: If we punish them for acting without orders, who will defend the border tomorrow?

sentences.zh: 願兩置賞刑，略而不問。」

translations.literal: I wish both reward and punishment set aside and broadly not pursued."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that both reward and punishment be set aside and the matter dropped."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 出鎮高陽八年，累加顯謨閣待制、直學士，徙知太原府，以疾，提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: After eight years governing Gaoyang, he was cumulatively made Attendant Gentleman of the Xianmo Pavilion and Direct Academician; moved to Taiyuan; on illness, put in charge of Dongxiao Palace.
