translations.idiomatic: He governed Gaoyang for eight years, rose to Attendant Gentleman of the Xianmo Pavilion and Direct Academician, then became prefect of Taiyuan; illness led to his appointment as superintendent of Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 先，承詔買馬三千給牧戶，近悉斂諸民而不予直，為御史所劾，失學士。

translations.literal: Previously, receiving an edict to buy three thousand horses for herders, Jin wholly exacted them from the people without payment; impeached by censors, he lost his academician title.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, ordered to purchase three thousand horses for pastoral households, he had requisitioned them from commoners without compensation; censors impeached him and he lost his academician rank.

sentences.zh: 二年而復之。

translations.literal: Two years later it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 鄭僅，字彥能，徐州彭城人。

translations.literal: Zheng Jin, style Yanneng, was a native of Pengcheng in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jin, courtesy name Yanneng, was from Pengcheng in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 第進士，為大名府司戶參軍。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as Records Clerk of Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi graduate, he served as revenue clerk of Daming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 留守文彥博以為材，部使者檄往他郡，彥博曰：「如鄭參軍詎可令數出？」

translations.literal: Keeper Wen Yanbo regarded him as talented; the circuit commissioner summoned him to another prefecture; Yanbo said: "How can one like Clerk Zheng be sent out repeatedly?"
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural commissioner Wen Yanbo prized his ability; when the circuit intendant tried to transfer him elsewhere Yanbo protested: "How can an officer like Clerk Zheng be shuffled about so often?"

sentences.zh: 奏改司法，遷冠氏令。

translations.literal: He memorialized to change him to judicial office; promoted to Magistrate of Guanshi.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to keep him for judicial work and had him promoted to magistrate of Guanshi.

sentences.zh: 河決府西，檄夜下調夫急，僅方閱保甲，盡籍即行，先他邑至，決遂塞。

translations.literal: The Yellow River burst west of the prefecture; a dispatch came at night urgently calling corvée; Jin was reviewing baojia registers, mustered all on the rolls and marched—arriving before other counties; the breach was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River broke west of the prefecture an urgent night dispatch called for laborers; Jin was reviewing household registers, mobilized every name on the rolls at once, reached the site ahead of neighboring counties, and the breach was sealed.

sentences.zh: 使者怒劾之，留守王拱辰爭於朝曰：「微冠氏，城民魚矣。」

translations.literal: The commissioner angrily impeached him; Keeper Wang Gongchen argued at court: "Without Guanshi, the city people would have been fish [drowned]."
translations.idiomatic: The intendant impeached him in anger, but prefect Wang Gongchen told the court: "Without Guanshi's men the city dwellers would have drowned like fish."

sentences.zh: 猶坐罰金。

translations.literal: He still suffered a fine.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was fined nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 時河朔饑，盜起，獨冠氏無之，且不入境。

translations.literal: When Hebei north was famished and bandits arose, only Guanshi had none and they did not even enter its border.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hebei famine bandits ravaged the region, but Guanshi alone was untouched—they would not even cross its border.

sentences.zh: 他邑獲盜，詰治之，盜因言：「鄭冠氏仁，故相戒不犯爾。」

translations.literal: Other counties caught bandits and interrogated them; the bandits said: "Magistrate Zheng of Guanshi is benevolent, so we mutually warned not to violate it."
translations.idiomatic: When other counties captured robbers the prisoners explained: "Magistrate Zheng of Guanshi is humane, so we warned one another not to raid his district."

sentences.zh: 知福昌縣，復值歲饑，悉意振貸，民不流亡。

translations.literal: Made Magistrate of Fuchang; again encountered famine—he devoted full effort to relief loans and the people did not flee.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Fuchang he again faced famine and spent all resources on relief grain loans, so the populace did not flee.

sentences.zh: 當第賞，不肯自列。

translations.literal: He ought to have ranked for reward but refused to list himself.
translations.idiomatic: He merited a merit citation but declined to nominate himself.

sentences.zh: 提舉京東常平，入為戶部員外郎，至太府卿，加直龍圖閣，為陝西都轉運使。

translations.literal: Commissioner for Jingdong Constant Granary; entered as Vice Director of Revenue, to Director of the Palace Granary; added Direct Dragon Diagram Pavilion; became Shaanxi Chief Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised the Jingdong granary, entered the capital as Vice Director and then Director of the Palace Granary, gained the Direct Dragon Diagram Pavilion title, and became chief transport commissioner for Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 論饋餉河湟功，進集賢殿修撰、顯謨閣待制。

translations.literal: For services in supplying grain to Huang and Zhuo, advanced to Academician Editor and Attendant Gentleman of Xianmo Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: For supplying the Hehuang campaigns he was promoted to Academician Editor and Attendant Gentleman of the Xianmo Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 僅請籍閉田為官莊，是歲，鎮戎、德順收谷十余萬。

translations.literal: Jin requested registering idle land as government estates; that year Zhenrong and Deshun harvested over a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed registering fallow land as state farms; that year Zhenrong and Deshun collected more than a hundred thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 會西寧高永年戰沒熙河，帥臣歸咎官莊奪屬羌地，致其怨畔，詔罷之，議者以為惜。

translations.literal: When Gao Yongnian of Xining died in battle in Hehuang, commanders blamed the government estates for seizing Qiang lands and causing their resentment and rebellion; an edict abolished them; deliberators thought it a pity.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao Yongnian of Xining fell in the Hehuang fighting, frontier commanders blamed the state farms for alienating Qiang lands and provoking revolt; the farms were abolished by edict, to the regret of many officials.

sentences.zh: 改知慶州，諸軍多殺老弱，持首要賞。

translations.literal: Transferred to Qingzhou; many troops killed old and weak, holding heads to claim reward.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Qingzhou he found troops often killed the elderly and weak and presented heads for bounty.

sentences.zh: 僅下令非強壯而能生致者，賞半之。

translations.literal: Jin ordered: those not strong and vigorous but brought in alive—half the reward.
translations.idiomatic: He decreed that captives who were not able-bodied fighting men but were taken alive would earn only half the standard reward.

sentences.zh: 有內附羌追寇，得老人，不忍殺，擒之，乃其父也，相持哭，一軍感動。

translations.literal: An affiliated Qiang pursued bandits, captured an old man, could not bear to kill—seized him and it was his father; they clung weeping; the whole army was moved.
translations.idiomatic: One assimilated Qiang pursuing bandits seized an old man he could not bring himself to kill—it proved to be his father; father and son wept in each other's arms and the entire unit was moved.

sentences.zh: 時諸路爭進討奏捷，僅獨保境不生事，寇亦不犯。

translations.literal: When all circuits competed to advance attacks and report victory, Jin alone kept the border unmolested; bandits also did not violate.
translations.idiomatic: While other circuits vied to raid and report victories, Jin alone held his line without provocation, and raiders in turn left his territory alone.

sentences.zh: 徙秦州，復為都轉運使，召拜戶部侍郎，改吏部侍郎、知徐州。

translations.literal: Moved to Qinzhou, again Chief Transport Commissioner; summoned as Vice Minister of Revenue, changed to Vice Minister of Personnel and prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He transferred to Qinzhou and again served as chief transport commissioner, then was recalled as Vice Minister of Revenue and later Vice Minister of Personnel and prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 以顯謨閣直學士、通議大夫卒，年六十七，贈光祿大夫，諡曰修敏。

translations.literal: Died as Direct Gentleman of Xianmo Pavilion and Grandee of Dawn Discussion, aged sixty-seven; posthumously made Grandee of Splendid Happiness, posthumous title Xiumin.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-seven as Direct Gentleman of the Xianmo Pavilion and Grandee of Dawn Discussion; posthumously honored as Grandee of Splendid Happiness with the posthumous name Xiumin.

sentences.zh: 子望之，自有傳。

translations.literal: Son Wangzhi has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wangzhi is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 宇文昌齡

translations.literal: Section heading: Yu Wenchangling
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenchangling

sentences.zh: 宇文昌齡，字伯修，成都雙流人。

translations.literal: Yu Wenchangling, style Boxiu, was a native of Shuangliu in Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenchangling, courtesy name Boxiu, was from Shuangliu in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 進士甲科，調榮州推官。

translations.literal: Jinshi first class; assigned as investigating officer of Rongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A first-class jinshi, he was appointed investigating officer in Rongzhou.

sentences.zh: 熊本經制梓夔，辟幹當公事。

translations.literal: Xiong Ben directed Zi and Kui circuits and recruited him as handler of public affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiong Ben pacified Zi and Kui circuits he recruited Changling as staff officer for public affairs.

sentences.zh: 凡攻討招襲，建南平諸城砦，皆出其畫。

translations.literal: All attacks, summons, raids, and building fortresses in Nanping came from his planning.
translations.idiomatic: Every campaign of attack, summons, and raid, and every fortress built in Nanping, followed plans he drew up.

sentences.zh: 遷大理丞。

translations.literal: Promoted to Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 本歸闕，言其功，擢提舉秦鳳路常平，改兩浙。

translations.literal: Ben returned to court, spoke of his merit; promoted Commissioner for Qinfeng Constant Granary, changed to Liangzhe.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiong Ben returned to court he praised Changling's service; Changling was made commissioner of the Qinfeng granary and later transferred to the Two Zhes.

sentences.zh: 神宗患司農圖籍不肅，選官厘整，昌齡以使夔路入辭，留為寺主簿，遂拜監察御史。

translations.literal: Shenzong worried Ministry of Revenue registers were disorderly, selected officials to reorganize; Changling entering to bid farewell for Kui circuit mission was kept as temple registrar, then made Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong, troubled by chaotic Ministry of Revenue records, chose officials to reorganize them; Changling, bidding farewell before a Kui mission, was retained as registrar of the ministry temple and soon appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 鄜延帥奏所部劉紹能與西羌通，將為患。

translations.literal: The Fuyan-Yan commander reported Liu Shaoneng of his command communicated with Western Qiang and would become a menace.
translations.idiomatic: The Fuyan-Yan frontier commander reported that Liu Shaoneng under his command was colluding with western Qiang and would become dangerous.

sentences.zh: 帝察其不然，命昌齡即鄜州鞫之，果妄也。

translations.literal: The emperor saw it was not so, ordered Changling immediately to Fuzhou to investigate—it proved false.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor doubted the charge and sent Changling straight to Fuzhou to investigate; the accusation proved groundless.

sentences.zh: 昌齡因請深戒守臣，毋生事徼賞，以靖邊人之心。

translations.literal: Changling therefore requested stern warning to border guardians not to stir trouble for reward, to settle border people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Changling then urged the court to warn frontier officials sternly against provoking incidents for merit and to reassure border populations.

sentences.zh: 使還，賜五品服。

translations.literal: Mission returned; granted fifth-rank robe.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was granted fifth-rank court robes.

sentences.zh: 尚書省建，以為比部員外郎。

translations.literal: When the Ministry Supervisory Office was established, made Vice Director of the Revenue Review Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When the new Ministry Supervisory Office was formed he was made vice director of the Revenue Review Bureau.

sentences.zh: 時官曹更新，統紀未立，昌齡悉力從事，雖抵暮亦程吏不止。

translations.literal: Offices newly renewed, regulations not yet set—Changling devoted full effort; even reaching evening he pressed clerks without stop.
translations.idiomatic: With offices reorganized but rules still unsettled, he threw himself into the work and kept clerks at their desks late into the evening.

sentences.zh: 具所立綱要，請於朝而行之。

translations.literal: He compiled the guidelines established and requested the court enact them.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted a full set of regulations and petitioned the throne to adopt them.

sentences.zh: 三司故吏狃玩弛，多不便，思有以中之。

translations.literal: Old clerks of the three commissions were accustomed to laxity, many inconvenienced, sought means to strike at him.
translations.idiomatic: Veteran clerks of the former Three Commissions, used to lax practice, resented the changes and looked for ways to undermine him.

sentences.zh: 擿邏卒糾其宿直遣小吏取衾服事，大臣欲論以私役，帝以職事修飭，釋不問。

translations.literal: Patrol soldiers exposed that on night duty he sent a petty clerk to fetch bedding—great ministers wished to charge private service; the emperor because duties were well regulated, released without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Patrol guards reported that during night watch he sent a junior clerk for bedding; senior officials wanted to charge him with misuse of labor, but the emperor, noting his offices were well run, dismissed the complaint.

sentences.zh: 改吏部員外郎，出京西轉運副使，召為左司員外郎。

translations.literal: Changed to Vice Director of Personnel; out as Western Capital Transport Vice Commissioner; summoned as Left Bureau Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He became Vice Director of Personnel, served as deputy transport commissioner for the western capital circuit, and was recalled as vice director of the Left Bureau.

sentences.zh: 送遼使至雄州，當宴，從者不待揖而坐，昌齡誚其使曰：「兩朝聘好百年矣，入境置宴，非但今日，揖而後坐，此禮渠可闕邪？」

translations.literal: Escorting Liao envoys to Xiongzhou, at the banquet their attendants sat without waiting for the bow; Changling reproached the envoy: "Our two courts have been friendly for a hundred years; banquets on entering the border are not only today's affair—bow then sit: can this ritual be omitted?"
translations.idiomatic: While escorting Liao envoys to Xiongzhou, at the feast their followers sat without bowing first; Changling rebuked the envoy: "Our states have been at peace for a century; welcoming banquets at the border are nothing new—bow, then be seated. How can that courtesy be skipped?"

sentences.zh: 使者陽若不服，而心悟其非，卒成禮去。

translations.literal: The envoy outwardly seemed unconvinced but inwardly knew his error; in the end the rites were completed and he departed.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy feigned offense but inwardly acknowledged the fault; the ceremony was completed properly and they departed.

sentences.zh: 遷太常少卿，詔議郊祀合祭，論者不一。

translations.literal: Promoted Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; an edict ordered discussion of combined suburban sacrifice; debaters were not united.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and ordered to debate whether heaven and earth should be worshipped together at the suburban altar; opinion was divided.

sentences.zh: 昌齡曰：「天地之數，以高卑則異位，以禮制則異宜，以樂舞則異數，至於衣服之章，器用之具，日至之時，皆有辨而不亂。

translations.literal: Changling said: "Heaven and earth in number, by high and low differ in position; by ritual system differ in propriety; by music and dance differ in number; down to insignia of dress, implements used, and the day of solstice—all have distinctions and are not confused.
translations.idiomatic: Changling argued: "Heaven and earth differ in rank and therefore in ritual form, in the number of dancers, in vestments and vessels, and even in the calendar day of sacrifice—each has its proper distinction.

sentences.zh: 夫祀者自有以感於無，自實以通於虛，必以類應類，以氣合氣，合然後可以得而親，可以冀其格。

translations.literal: Sacrifice has its own means of moving from being to non-being, from solid to penetrating the void—categories must respond to categories, qi must join qi; only then can one draw near and hope for presence.
translations.idiomatic: Worship moves from the manifest to the unseen and from substance to spirit; like must answer like and breath must meet breath—only then can the sacrificer approach and hope for a response.

sentences.zh: 今祭地於圜丘，以氣則非所合，以類則非所應，而求高厚之來享，不亦難乎。」

translations.literal: Now to sacrifice earth at the round mound—in qi it is not what joins, in category it is not what responds—and yet seek the high and thick to come enjoy: is it not difficult?
translations.idiomatic: To offer earth at the round Altar of Heaven is neither a joining of qi nor a matching of kinds, yet expect Heaven and Earth to accept the offering—is that not vain?

sentences.zh: 後竟用其議。

translations.literal: In the end his argument was used.
translations.idiomatic: The court eventually adopted his view.

sentences.zh: 改直秘閣、知梓州，曆壽州、河中府、鄧、鄆、青三州。

translations.literal: Changed to Direct Secret Pavilion, prefect of Zizhou; successively governed Shouzhou, Hezhong Prefecture, and the three prefectures of Deng, Yan, and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: He became Direct Gentleman of the Secret Pavilion and prefect of Zizhou, then served successively at Shouzhou, Hezhong, and the prefectures of Deng, Yan, and Qing.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，召為刑部侍郎，徙戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Huizong ascended, summoned as Vice Minister of Justice, moved to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong took the throne he was recalled as Vice Minister of Justice and then transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 陝西饋芻糧于邊，舊制令內郡轉給，為民病。

translations.literal: Shaanxi supplied fodder and grain to the border; the old system ordered inner circuits to relay it—a hardship for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi fed fodder and grain to the frontier; the old rule required interior prefectures to forward supplies, which burdened the populace.

sentences.zh: 昌齡建言止輸其州，而令量取道裏費助邊糴，從之。

translations.literal: Changling memorialized to stop shipping grain from his prefecture alone, and instead to measure road-mile costs to assist border grain purchases; it was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Changling proposed halting each prefecture's full relay obligation and instead assessing transport costs by distance to subsidize frontier grain buying, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 歲省糴價五百萬，公私便之。

translations.literal: Each year it saved five million in grain-purchase prices; public and private alike found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The change saved five million in annual grain costs and eased the burden on both government and people.

sentences.zh: 以寶文閣待制知開封府，復為戶部侍郎，知青、杭、越三州。

translations.literal: With the title of Baowen Pavilion attendant-drafter he governed Kaifeng Prefecture, again became Vice Minister of Revenue, and held Qing, Hang, and Yue prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Kaifeng with the rank of attendant-drafter in the Baowen Pavilion, returned to the post of Vice Minister of Revenue, and governed Qingzhou, Hangzhou, and Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十五，詔為封傅護送歸，官給其葬費。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-five; an edict ordered Feng Fu to escort the coffin home, and the government supplied funeral expenses.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-five. The throne ordered Feng Fu to escort his remains home and paid the funeral costs from the public purse.

sentences.zh: 子常。

translations.literal: His son was Chang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang.

sentences.zh: 子 常

translations.literal: Son: Chang
translations.idiomatic: His son, Chang

sentences.zh: 常字權可。

translations.literal: Chang was styled Quanke.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, whose style name was Quanke.

sentences.zh: 政和末，知黎州。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenghe era he governed Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Near the close of the Zhenghe reign he was prefect of Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 有上書乞於大渡河外置城邑以便互市者，詔以訪常。

translations.literal: Someone memorialized asking to build cities and towns beyond the Dadu River to facilitate mutual trade; an edict ordered that Chang be consulted.
translations.idiomatic: A memorial asked to establish towns beyond the Dadu River to ease border trade, and the court instructed that Chang be consulted.

sentences.zh: 常言：「自孟氏入朝，藝祖取蜀輿地圖觀之，畫大渡為境，曆百五十年無西南夷患。

translations.literal: Chang said: "Since the Meng clan submitted to the court, the Founder took out the Shu territorial map and looked at it, drawing the Dadu as the border; for one hundred fifty years there has been no trouble from southwestern Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "After the Meng submitted, our Founder studied the map of Shu and marked the Dadu as the frontier; for a century and a half the southwest has been free of barbarian trouble.

sentences.zh: 今若於河外建城立邑，虜情攜貳，邊隙寢開，非中國之福也。」

translations.literal: If now cities and towns are built and established beyond the river, barbarian hearts will grow divided in loyalty, border gaps will gradually open, and this is not a blessing for China."
translations.idiomatic: Building settlements beyond the river would sow divided loyalties among the tribes and slowly reopen the frontier—no blessing for the realm."

sentences.zh: 尋提舉成都路茶馬。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was made commissioner of the Chengdu circuit tea-and-horse trade.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon appointed him to supervise the Chengdu circuit tea-and-horse offices.

sentences.zh: 自熙、豐以來，歲入馬蕃多；

translations.literal: From the Xi and Feng years onward, horses brought in yearly from the Fan were many;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Xi and Feng reforms the yearly intake of Tibetan horses had been plentiful;

sentences.zh: 至崇、觀間，其法始壞。

translations.literal: by the Chong and Guan period the system first broke down.
translations.idiomatic: but by the Chongning and Guanning era the system had begun to collapse.

sentences.zh: 提舉官歲以所入進羨餘，吏緣為奸，市馬裁十一二，且負其直，夷人皆怨。

translations.literal: The commissioners each year reported the intake as surplus tribute; clerks used this as a pretext for fraud, buying horses only one or two in ten, and still owing the price—so the Yi peoples were all resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioners annually padded their accounts with reported surpluses; clerks turned the practice to fraud, purchasing barely a tenth of the horses owed and even defaulting on payment, until the tribes were seething.

sentences.zh: 常盡革其弊，馬遂溢額。

translations.literal: Chang completely reformed these abuses, and horses then exceeded the quota.
translations.idiomatic: Chang swept away the abuses, and horse deliveries soon surpassed the quota.

sentences.zh: 加直秘閣，改知夔州，進秘閣修撰。

translations.literal: He was given the rank of Direct Associate of the Secretariat Pavilion, transferred to govern Kuizhou, and advanced to Secretariat Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to direct associate of the Secretariat Pavilion, made prefect of Kuizhou, and then advanced to compiler in the same pavilion.

sentences.zh: 官累中大夫。

translations.literal: His offices accumulated to Grandee of Palace Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Grandee of Palace Attendance.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 許幾，字先之，信州貴溪人。

translations.literal: Xu Ji, styled Xianzhi, was a native of Guixi in Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ji, whose style name was Xianzhi, came from Guixi in Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 少以諸生謁韓琦于魏，琦勉入太學。

translations.literal: In youth, as a student, he visited Han Qi in Wei; Qi urged him to enter the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: As a young scholar he called on Han Qi in Wei, and Qi encouraged him to enroll in the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 擢第，調高安、樂平主簿，知南陵縣，還民之托僧尼為奸者數百人。

translations.literal: He passed the examination, was posted as registrar of Gaoxan and Leping, governed Nanling County, and returned to the people several hundred who had entrusted monks and nuns to commit fraud.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he served as registrar in Gaoxan and Leping and as magistrate of Nanling, where he restored to commoners several hundred families whose property had been seized through monastic fraud.

sentences.zh: 提舉京西常平，為開封府推官，進至將作監。

translations.literal: He was commissioner of the Western Capital Ever-Normal Granaries, became a judicial investigator in the Kaifeng prefectural office, and advanced to Director of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised Ever-Normal Granaries on the western capital circuit, served as a judicial investigator in Kaifeng, and rose to director of the Directorate of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 吏與匠比為奸欺，凡斫削、塗塈、丹雘之工當以次用，而始役即概給其稟，費亡藝而患不均。

translations.literal: Clerks and craftsmen colluded in fraud: all work of hewing, plastering, and cinnabar lacquer should be used in sequence, yet at the start of labor lump-sum rations were given, waste exceeded all bounds, and there was worry over unevenness.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks and artisans had colluded in fraud: hewing, plastering, and lacquering were supposed to be paid in stages, but rations were issued in lump sums at the outset, wasting funds without limit and breeding unfairness.

sentences.zh: 幾逆為之程，費省工倍。

translations.literal: Ji inversely set procedures for it; costs were saved and work doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Ji reversed the practice by setting staged schedules, cutting costs while doubling output.

sentences.zh: 再遷太僕卿、戶部侍郎，以顯謨閣待制知鄆州。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Grand Mentor of the Stud and Vice Minister of Revenue, and with the title of Xianmo Pavilion attendant-drafter governed Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Grand Mentor of the Stud and Vice Minister of Revenue, then sent to Yanzhou as attendant-drafter of the Xianmo Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 梁山濼多盜，皆漁者窟穴也。

translations.literal: Liangshan Marsh had many bandits; all were dens of fishermen.
translations.idiomatic: Liangshan Marsh teemed with bandits who hid among the fishing villages.

sentences.zh: 幾籍十人為保，使晨出夕歸，否則以告，輒窮治，無脫者。

translations.literal: Ji registered ten men as a mutual-guarantee unit, made them go out in the morning and return in the evening; otherwise they were reported, and he then prosecuted to the end—none escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Ji grouped fishermen in tens under mutual surety, requiring them to put out at dawn and return at dusk; violators were reported and prosecuted without exception.

sentences.zh: 幾有吏幹，善理財，由是四入戶部至尚書。

translations.literal: Ji had bureaucratic talent and was skilled at managing finances; because of this he four times entered the Ministry of Revenue up to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had a gift for administration and finance and served four terms in the Ministry of Revenue, rising to minister.

sentences.zh: 嘗以搖泉布法罷，又以治染院事失實，知婺州。

translations.literal: He was once dismissed for swaying the coin-and-cloth law, and again for handling affairs of the dyeing office untruthfully; he governed Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was once removed over interference with coinage and cloth currency regulations, and later faulted for mishandling the imperial dye works before being made prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 進樞密直學士、河北都轉運使、徙知成德軍、知太原府。

translations.literal: He advanced to Privy Council academician, Hebei transport commissioner, was moved to govern the Chengde army, and governed Taiyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He became a privy council academician and chief transport commissioner for Hebei, then governed the Chengde garrison and Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 張商英裁損吏祿，幾預其議，貶永州團練副使，安置袁州。

translations.literal: Zhang Shangying cut official salaries; Ji took part in the deliberation and was demoted to training vice commissioner of Yongzhou and settled at Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shangying slashed official salaries Ji joined the debate and was demoted to training vice commissioner at Yongzhou and exiled to Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 遇恩，復中大夫，卒。

translations.literal: He met an amnesty, was restored to Grandee of Palace Attendance, and died.
translations.idiomatic: After a general amnesty he was restored to Grandee of Palace Attendance, then died.

sentences.zh: 程之邵

translations.literal: Cheng Zhi Shao
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Zhi Shao

sentences.zh: 程之邵，字懿叔，眉州眉山人。

translations.literal: Cheng Zhi Shao, styled Yishu, was a native of Meishan in Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Zhi Shao, style name Yishu, was born in Meishan, Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖仁霸，治獄有陰德。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Renba, in handling cases, had hidden virtue.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Renba had earned quiet merit through merciful judgment in criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 之邵以父蔭為新繁主簿。

translations.literal: Zhi Shao, through his father's yin privilege, became registrar of Xinfan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Shao entered service through his father's privilege as registrar of Xinfan.

sentences.zh: 熙寧更募役法，常平使者欲概州縣民力，以羨乏相補。

translations.literal: In the Xining reforms of the corvée-recruitment law, the Ever-Normal envoy wished to lump together the labor power of prefectures and counties and use surplus and deficit to supplement one another.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xining corvée reforms were introduced, the Ever-Normal commissioner wanted to pool labor levies across counties and offset surpluses against shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 之邵曰：「此法乃成周均力遺意，當各以一邑之力供一邑之役，豈宜以此邑助他邑哉？」

translations.literal: Zhi Shao said: "This law is the surviving intent of the Zhou in equalizing labor power; each district should supply one district's corvée with its own strength—how can one district be used to aid another?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Shao said, "The reform follows the Zhou ideal of equal labor: each community should bear its own corvée. How can one district be made to serve another?"

sentences.zh: 使者愧服，辟之邵為屬，聽其所為。

translations.literal: The envoy was ashamed and submitted; he recruited Zhi Shao as an aide and let him act as he wished.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy accepted the rebuke, took Zhi Shao on as aide, and left implementation to him.

sentences.zh: 熊本察訪蜀道歸，語諸朝曰：「役法初行，成都路為最詳，之邵力也。」

translations.literal: Xiong Ben, on returning from inspecting the Shu roads, told the court: "When the corvée law was first carried out, the Chengdu circuit was the most thorough—it was Zhi Shao's effort."
translations.idiomatic: After inspecting the Shu routes, Xiong Ben told the court, "When the corvée law first took effect, the Chengdu circuit was the best run—thanks to Zhi Shao."

sentences.zh: 詔召見，成都守趙抃奏留之。

translations.literal: An edict summoned him for audience; the Chengdu prefect Zhao Bian memorialized to retain him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered him to court, but Chengdu's prefect Zhao Bian memorialized to keep him in the southwest.

sentences.zh: 入為三司磨勘官，得隱匿數十萬緡。

translations.literal: He entered as an auditor of the Three Commissions and uncovered several hundred thousand strings of concealed cash.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he audited the Three Commissions and exposed several hundred thousand strings of hidden funds.

sentences.zh: 從副使蹇周輔計度江、嶺鹽，還，除廣東轉運判官。

translations.literal: He followed Vice Commissioner Jian Zhoufu in surveying Jiang and Ling salt, returned, and was appointed transport judge of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He assisted Vice Commissioner Jian Zhoufu in surveying salt along the Yangzi and Lingnan, then returned to become transport judge of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，提舉利、梓路常平，周輔得罪，亦罷知祥符縣。

translations.literal: At the start of Yuanyou he was commissioner of Ever-Normal Granaries on the Li and Zi circuits; Zhoufu offended and was punished, and he too was dismissed to govern Xiangfu County.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanyou he oversaw Ever-Normal Granaries on the Li and Zi circuits; when Zhoufu fell from favor he was demoted to magistrate of Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 俄知泗州，為夔路轉運判官。

translations.literal: Soon he governed Sizhou and became transport judge of the Kuilu circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made prefect of Sizhou and transport judge on the Kuizhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 夔守強狠不奉法，劾正其罪。

translations.literal: The Kuizhou prefect was fierce and unyielding and did not follow the law; he impeached and corrected his crime.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Kuizhou was brutal and lawless; Zhi Shao impeached him and secured conviction.

sentences.zh: 大寧井鹽為利博，前議者輒儲其半供公上，余鬻於民，使先輸錢，鹽不足給，民以病告。

translations.literal: Daning well salt yielded great profit; previous planners always stored half to supply the public treasury, sold the remainder to the people requiring advance payment of money—when salt was insufficient to deliver, the people reported hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Daning's well salt was highly profitable; earlier planners hoarded half for the state and sold the rest only on prepayment, so short deliveries drove the people to complain of hardship.

sentences.zh: 之邵盡發所儲與之，商賈既通，關征增數倍。

translations.literal: Zhi Shao fully released what was stored and gave it out; once merchants flowed, pass duties increased several fold.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Shao released the entire reserve to the market; trade revived and transit duties multiplied several times over.

sentences.zh: 除主管秦、蜀茶馬公事，革黎州買馬之弊，歲以仲秋為市，市四月止，以羨茶入熙、秦易戰騎，得良馬益多。

translations.literal: He was appointed to supervise Qin and Shu tea-and-horse affairs, reformed the abuses of horse-buying in Lizhou, each year taking mid-autumn as the market, the market stopping after four months, using surplus tea sent into Xi and Qin to exchange for war mounts, and obtaining good horses in ever greater numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Put in charge of Qin and Shu tea-and-horse trade, he reformed Lizhou's horse purchases by fixing a four-month autumn market and trading surplus tea in Xi and Qin for cavalry mounts, steadily increasing the intake of fine horses.

sentences.zh: 知鳳翔府，民負債無以償，自焚其居，而紿曰遺火；

translations.literal: He governed Fengxiang Prefecture; people who owed debts and could not repay burned their own dwellings and deceived others, saying it was a leftover fire;
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Fengxiang he found debtors who could not pay setting fire to their homes and claiming accidental blaze;

sentences.zh: 有主藏吏殺四婢，人無知者。

translations.literal: there was a treasury clerk who killed four maidservants, and no one knew.
translations.idiomatic: and a treasury clerk who murdered four maidservants without anyone's knowledge.

sentences.zh: 之邵發擿，岐人傳誦。

translations.literal: Zhi Shao exposed and rooted them out; the people of Qi spread the story in recitation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Shao uncovered both cases, and the people of the Qishan region passed the tales from mouth to mouth.

sentences.zh: 徙鄭州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His next post was Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 元符中復主管茶馬，市馬至萬匹，得茶課四百萬緡。

translations.literal: In the Yuanfu era he again supervised tea and horses; horses traded reached ten thousand, and tea tax yielded four million strings.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanfu he again headed the tea-and-horse offices, trading up to ten thousand horses and yielding four million strings in tea revenue.

sentences.zh: 童貫用師熙、岷，不俟報，運茶往博糴，發錢二十萬億佐用度。

translations.literal: Tong Guan used troops in Xi and Min, did not wait for reports, transported tea to exchange for grain, and issued cash of two hundred myriads of yi to assist expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong Guan campaigned in Xi and Min he acted without awaiting approval, sent tea to barter for grain, and released two hundred thousand strings of cash to meet army expenses.

sentences.zh: 連加直龍圖閣、集賢殿修撰，三進秩，為熙河都轉運使。

translations.literal: He was successively given Direct Dragon Diagram Pavilion, Academician of the Hall for Collecting Treasures, three advances in rank, and became Xihe transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through direct associate of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and compiler in the Hall for Collecting Treasures across three promotions to chief transport commissioner of Xihe.

sentences.zh: 秦鳳出師，命之經制，即言已備十萬騎可食三百日矣。

translations.literal: When Qin and Feng sent out the army, he was ordered to control supplies; he immediately said he had already prepared for one hundred thousand riders to eat for three hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qin-Feng armies marched he was put in charge of logistics and at once reported stores enough to feed a hundred thousand horsemen for three hundred days.

sentences.zh: 徽宗喜，擢顯謨閣待制。

translations.literal: Huizong was pleased and promoted him to Xianmo Pavilion attendant-drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Huizong promoted him to attendant-drafter of the Xianmo Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 敵犯熙河，之邵攝帥事，屯兵行邊境，解去。

translations.literal: The enemy invaded Xihe; Zhi Shao acted as commander in the marshal's stead, stationed troops along the marching border, and the siege lifted.
translations.idiomatic: When enemies struck Xihe he acted as commander, posted troops along the frontier, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 俄得疾卒。

translations.literal: Soon he took ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 方錄功轉太中大夫，不及拜，贈龍圖閣直學士，官護喪歸。

translations.literal: Just as merit was being recorded to transfer him to Grandee of Palace Attendance, he had no time to receive the appointment; posthumously he was gifted Dragon Diagram Pavilion Direct Academician, and officials escorted the coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: Merit rolls were advancing him to Grandee of Palace Attendance when he died before taking office; the court posthumously granted him direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and sent officials to escort his coffin home.

sentences.zh: 子唐，至寶文閣學士。

translations.literal: His son Tang reached Baowen Pavilion academician.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tang rose to academician of the Baowen Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 龔原，字深之，處州遂昌人。

translations.literal: Gong Yuan, styled Shenzhi, was a native of Suichang in Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Yuan, style name Shenzhi, was from Suichang in Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 少與陸佃同師王安石。

translations.literal: In youth he and Lu Dian studied under the same teacher, Wang Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he studied under Wang Anshi together with Lu Dian.

sentences.zh: 進士高第，元豐中為國子直講，以虞蕃訟失官。

translations.literal: He placed high in the jinshi examination; in the Yuanfeng era he was a lecturer in the State University, and lost office because of Yu Fan's lawsuit.
translations.idiomatic: He graduated near the top of the jinshi rolls, lectured at the State University under Yuanfeng, and was dismissed after the Yu Fan litigation.

sentences.zh: 哲宗即位，詣訴理所得直，為國子丞、太常博士。

translations.literal: When Zhezong acceded, he went to appeal and straighten the matter, gaining reinstatement as State University vice director and Court of Sacrifices doctor.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhezong took the throne he appealed successfully and was restored as vice director of the State University and doctor of the Court of Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 方議祀北郊，原曰：「合祭，非理也。

translations.literal: Just as sacrifice at the northern suburb was being debated, Yuan said: "Combined sacrifice is not according to principle.
translations.idiomatic: When court debated the northern suburban rites, Yuan argued, "Combining the sacrifices is wrong in principle.

sentences.zh: 天子父天母地，既不為寒而廢祠，其可為暑而輟行？

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven takes Heaven as father and Earth as mother; since he does not abandon sacrifice because of cold, how can he stop the rite because of heat?
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven honors Heaven as father and Earth as mother; if cold does not cancel the rites, how can heat?

sentences.zh: 此漢儒陋說爾，願亟正之。」

translations.literal: This is merely the crude saying of Han Confucians; I hope it will quickly be corrected."
translations.idiomatic: That is a crude Han scholastic notion, and I urge the court to correct it at once."

sentences.zh: 加秘閣校理，充徐王府記室，出為兩浙轉運判官。

translations.literal: He was added as Secretariat proofreader, filled the post of recorder in the Xu Prince's household, and went out as transport judge of the Two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was made proofreader in the Secretariat, served as recorder in the household of Prince Xu, and was posted as transport judge on the Two Zhe circuits.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，召拜國子司業，入對，帝問曰：「卿曆徐邸官，何為補外，得非大臣私意乎？」

translations.literal: At the start of Shaosheng he was summoned and appointed State University vice rector; entering audience, the emperor asked: "You served in the Xu residence—why were you given an outside supplemental post? Surely this was not ministers' private intent?"
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shaosheng he was recalled as vice rector of the State University. At audience the emperor asked, "You served Prince Xu's household—why were you sent outside the capital? Was that a minister's private maneuver?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣出使鄉部，獲知民間事宜，臣素知如是，不知其因也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant went out to his home district and gained knowledge of folk affairs; your servant always knew it was thus, but does not know the reason."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "When I went home I learned the people's concerns firsthand. I had long suspected as much, though I do not know who arranged it."

sentences.zh: 旋兼侍講，遷秘書少監、起居舍人，權工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was concurrently lecturer, moved to Secretariat vice director, court diarist, and acting Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made concurrent lecturer, then Secretariat vice director, court diarist, and acting Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 為曾布所重，安惇論其直講時事，以集賢殿修撰知潤州。

translations.literal: He was valued by Zeng Bu; An Dun criticized affairs from his lecturer period, and he was made Academician of the Hall for Collecting Treasures and governed Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Bu favored him, but An Dun attacked his conduct as lecturer, and he was sent to Runzhou as compiler in the Hall for Collecting Treasures.

sentences.zh: 徽宗初，入為秘書監，進給事中。

translations.literal: At the start of Huizong he entered as Secretariat director and advanced to Censorate attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong took power he became director of the Secretariat and was promoted to attendant in the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 時除郎官五人，皆執政姻戚，悉舉駁之；

translations.literal: At that time five bureau officials were appointed, all kinsmen of the ruling ministers; he memorialized to reject them all;
translations.idiomatic: When five bureau posts went to ruling ministers' kin, he memorialized to block every appointment;

sentences.zh: 又論郝隨得罪，不得居京師，鄧洵武不宜再入史院。

translations.literal: he also argued that Hao Sui, having offended, must not dwell in the capital, and that Deng Xunwu was unsuitable to re-enter the History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: and argued that Hao Sui, having offended, should not remain in the capital and that Deng Xunwu ought not rejoin the History Institute.

sentences.zh: 朝論謂帝為哲宗服，當循開寶故事，為齊衰期。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that in mourning Zhezong the emperor should follow the Kaibao precedent and observe the one-year qi mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion held that mourning Zhezong required following the Kaibao precedent of one-year qi mourning.

sentences.zh: 原曰：「三年之喪，自天子達于庶人，一也。」

translations.literal: Yuan said: "The three-year mourning, from the Son of Heaven down to the common people, is one and the same."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan replied, "The three-year mourning applies alike from the Son of Heaven to the common people."

sentences.zh: 主議者斥其妄，黜知南康軍，改壽州。

translations.literal: The leaders of the debate denounced his rashness, demoted him to govern the Nankang army, and changed him to Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The majority denounced him as reckless, demoted him to the Nankang commandery, then transferred him to Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄用三年之制，乃復修撰，知揚州。

translations.literal: Soon the three-year system was adopted; he was then restored as compiler and governed Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the court soon adopted three-year mourning he was restored as compiler and made prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 還朝，曆兵、工部二侍郎，除寶文閣待制、知廬州。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he passed through the two vice ministries of War and Works, was removed as Baowen Pavilion attendant-drafter, and governed Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he served as vice minister of War and Works, then was made attendant-drafter of the Baowen Pavilion and prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 陳瓘擊蔡京，原與瓘善，或謂原實使之，奪職居和州。

translations.literal: Chen Guan attacked Cai Jing; Yuan was friendly with Guan, and some said Yuan had actually instigated him; his office was stripped and he dwelt at Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Guan assailed Cai Jing, Yuan's friendship with him led some to claim Yuan had orchestrated the attack; he was stripped of office and exiled to Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 起為亳州，命下而卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: He was raised to Bozhou; the order was issued but he died, age sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to Bozhou, but died at sixty-seven before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 初，王安石改學校法，引原自助，原亦為盡力。

translations.literal: Initially Wang Anshi reformed the school law and drew Yuan to assist himself; Yuan also exerted his utmost strength.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi reformed the schools he enlisted Yuan's help, and Yuan threw himself into the work.

sentences.zh: 其後，司馬光召與語，譏切王氏，原反覆辨救不少衰。

translations.literal: Afterward Sima Guang summoned him to speak, sharply criticizing the Wang clan; Yuan repeatedly defended and rescued them without lessening.
translations.idiomatic: Later Sima Guang summoned him and sharply attacked the Wang faction; Yuan argued back in their defense without yielding.

sentences.zh: 光歎曰：「王氏習氣尚爾邪！」

translations.literal: Guang sighed and said: "The habits of the Wang clan are still thus!"
translations.idiomatic: Guang sighed, "The Wang faction's habits die hard!"

sentences.zh: 為司業時，請以安石所撰《字說》、《洪範傳》及子雱《論語》、《孟子義》刊板傳學者。

translations.literal: As vice rector he requested that Anshi's Explanations of Characters and Commentary on the Hongfan, and his son Bian's Analects and Mencius Meanings, be carved on blocks and transmitted to scholars.
translations.idiomatic: As vice rector he asked that Wang's Explanations of Characters and Hongfan Commentary and his son Bian's commentaries on the Analects and Mencius be printed for students.

sentences.zh: 故一時學校舉子之文，靡然從之，其敝自原始。

translations.literal: Thus for a time the essays of school examinees all followed them in sway; the harm originated from Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Exam essays across the academies soon followed that fashion, and the damage began with Yuan.

sentences.zh: 崔公度

translations.literal: Cui Gongdu
translations.idiomatic: Cui Gongdu

sentences.zh: 崔公度，字伯易，高郵人。

translations.literal: Cui Gongdu, styled Boyi, was a native of Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Gongdu, style name Boyi, came from Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 口吃不能劇談，而內絕敏，書一閱即不忘。

translations.literal: He stammered and could not talk vigorously, yet inwardly was extremely sharp; a book once read he never forgot.
translations.idiomatic: A stammer kept him from fluent speech, but his mind was razor-sharp and he never forgot a book after one reading.

sentences.zh: 劉沆薦茂才異等，辭疾不應命。

translations.literal: Liu Kang recommended him as exceptional talent of a special grade; he declined on grounds of illness and did not answer the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kang nominated him for exceptional talent, but he pleaded illness and declined the summons.

sentences.zh: 用父任，補三班差使，非其好也，益閉戶讀書。

translations.literal: Through his father's appointment he filled the post of third-class envoy; it was not his liking, and he all the more shut his door and read books.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office through his father's privilege as a third-class envoy, disliked the post, and devoted himself ever more to study behind closed doors.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修得其所作《感山賦》，以示韓琦，琦上之英宗，即付史館。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu obtained his composition Ganshan Fu, showed it to Han Qi, and Qi submitted it to Yingzong; it was immediately sent to the History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu obtained his Ganshan Fu and showed it to Han Qi, who presented it to Yingzong; the emperor immediately sent it to the History Institute.

sentences.zh: 授和州防禦推官，為國子直講，以母老辭。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hezhou defense judicial investigator, became a State University lecturer, and declined because his mother was old.
translations.idiomatic: He was made judicial investigator at Hezhou and lecturer at the State University, but declined the latter because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 王安石當國，獻《熙甯稽古一法百利論》，安石解衣握手，延與語。

translations.literal: When Wang Anshi held the state, he submitted the Xining Examining Antiquity, One Law, Hundred Benefits treatise; Anshi removed his robe, clasped his hands, and prolonged conversation with him.
translations.idiomatic: With Wang Anshi in power he submitted his treatise One Law, Hundred Benefits under Xining's Return to Antiquity; Wang received him informally and talked at length.

sentences.zh: 召對延和殿，進光祿丞，知陽武縣。

translations.literal: He was summoned to audience in the Yanhe Hall, advanced to Guanglu Vice Director, and governed Yangwu County.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to audience in the Yanhe Hall, he was promoted to vice director of the Guanglu Office and made magistrate of Yangwu.

sentences.zh: 京官謁尹，故事當拜庭下，公度疑尹辱己，徑詣安石訴之，安石使鄧綰薦為御史。

translations.literal: When capital officials visited the prefect, by precedent they should bow in the courtyard; Gongdu suspected the prefect was insulting him, went straight to Anshi to complain, and Anshi had Deng Chuo recommend him as censor.
translations.idiomatic: Capital officials calling on the Kaifeng prefect were expected to bow in the courtyard; Gongdu took this as an insult, appealed directly to Wang Anshi, and Wang had Deng Chuo nominate him for the censorate.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為崇文校書，刪定三司令式，於是誦言京官庭謁尹非宜，安石為下編敕所更其制。

translations.literal: Before long he was made collator in the Chongwen office and revised the statutes of the three bureaus; he then spread word that it was improper for capital officials to bow in the courtyard before the prefect, and Anshi had the codification office change the regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became a Chongwen collator and revised the three bureaus' statutes; arguing that capital officials should not bow in the courtyard to the prefect, he persuaded Anshi to have the codifiers change the rule.

sentences.zh: 加集賢校理，知太常禮院。

translations.literal: He was added as collator in the Jixian office and made director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Jixian collator and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 公度起布衣，無所持守，惟知媚附安石，晝夜造請，雖踞廁見之，不屑也。

translations.literal: Gongdu rose from commoner status with nothing to uphold; he knew only how to flatter and cling to Anshi, calling on him day and night—even if Anshi received him while seated on the privy, he did not disdain it.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner with no principles, Gongdu knew only to fawn on Anshi, visiting day and night—even receiving audience on the privy without shame.

sentences.zh: 嘗從後執其帶尾，安石反顧，公度笑曰：「相公帶有垢，敬以袍拭去之爾。」

translations.literal: Once he followed from behind and seized the end of his belt; Anshi looked back and Gongdu smiled, saying, "Your belt has a stain—your servant respectfully wipes it away with his robe."
translations.idiomatic: Once he grabbed Anshi's belt from behind; when Anshi turned, Gongdu smiled: "Your belt is soiled—let me wipe it with my robe."

sentences.zh: 見者皆笑，亦恬不為恥。

translations.literal: Onlookers all laughed, yet he was calmly unashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Spectators laughed, but he felt no shame.

sentences.zh: 請知海州。

translations.literal: He requested appointment as prefect of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to be prefect of Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 元祐、紹聖之間，曆兵禮部郎中、國子司業，除秘書少監、起居郎，皆辭不受。

translations.literal: Between the Yuanyou and Shaosheng reigns he served as bureau director in the Ministries of War and Rites and as vice director of the National University; appointments as vice director of the Secretariat and court attendant were all declined.
translations.idiomatic: Between Yuanyou and Shaosheng he served in the war and rites ministries and as National University vice director, but declined posts as Secretariat vice director and court attendant.

sentences.zh: 知潁、潤、宣、通四州，以直龍圖閣卒。

translations.literal: He governed the four prefectures of Ying, Run, Xuan, and Tong, and died as Longtu Pavilion academician-at-large.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Ying, Run, Xuan, and Tong prefectures and died as a Longtu Pavilion academician-at-large.

sentences.zh: 蒲卣，字君錫，閬州人。

translations.literal: Pu You, styled Junxi, was a native of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pu You, courtesy name Junxi, came from Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 母任知書，裏中號「任五經」，卣幼以開敏聞。

translations.literal: His mother Ren was learned in books and was called in the neighborhood "Ren of the Five Classics"; You was known in youth for quick intelligence.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Ren was learned and called "Ren of the Five Classics" locally; You was known from childhood for sharp intelligence.

sentences.zh: 中進士第，曆利州司戶參軍、三泉主簿、知合江金水縣。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as revenue clerk in Lizhou, registrar of Sanquan, and magistrate of Hejiang Jinshui county.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi graduate, he served as Lizhou revenue clerk, Sanquan registrar, and magistrate of Hejiang Jinshui.

sentences.zh: 通判文州，有獻議者欲開文州徑路達陝西，卣言：「洮、岷、積石至文為甚邇，自文出江油，鄧艾取蜀故道也。

translations.literal: As vice-prefect of Wenzhou someone proposed opening a direct route from Wenzhou to Shaanxi; You said, "From Tao, Min, and Jishi to Wen is very close; from Wen out through Jiangyou is the old road by which Deng Ai took Shu.
translations.idiomatic: As Wenzhou vice-prefect, when someone proposed a direct route to Shaanxi, You said, "Tao, Min, and Jishi lie very near Wen; the road from Wen through Jiangyou is Deng Ai's old invasion route into Shu.

sentences.zh: 異時鬼章欲從此窺蜀，為其阻隘而止。

translations.literal: In former times Gui Zhang wished to spy on Shu from here but stopped because of its narrow passes.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Zhang once tried to probe Shu this way but was stopped by the narrow terrain.

sentences.zh: 夏人志此久矣，可為之通道乎？」

translations.literal: The Western Xia have long coveted this—can we open a road for them?"
translations.idiomatic: The Western Xia have coveted this route for ages—should we open it for them?"

sentences.zh: 議遂塞。

translations.literal: The proposal was then blocked.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal died.

sentences.zh: 為睦親宅教授，提舉湖北、京西常平。

translations.literal: He was instructor at the Mansion of Cordial Kinship and put in charge of the Hubei and Jingxi granary systems.
translations.idiomatic: He taught at the Mansion of Cordial Kinship and oversaw the Hubei and Jingxi granary systems.

sentences.zh: 崇甯均田，轉運使以用不足，將度費以定稅，卣曰：「詔旨所以嘉惠元元爾，初不在增賦也。」

translations.literal: Under Chongning's equal-field policy the transport commissioner, finding funds insufficient, planned to measure expenses to set taxes; You said, "The edict's purpose was to benefit the common people—it was never about increasing levies."
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongning equal-field reforms the transport commissioner, short of funds, planned to set taxes by measuring costs; You said, "The edict aimed to benefit the people, not to raise taxes."

sentences.zh: 宛、穰地廣沃，國初募民墾田，得為世業，令人毋輒訴，蓋百年矣，好訟者稍以易佃法搖之，卣一切禁止。

translations.literal: Wan and Xiang lands are broad and fertile; at the dynasty's founding commoners were recruited to open fields and could hold them as hereditary property, with suits forbidden—this had stood for a century; litigious men began to shake this with tenant-exchange laws, and You forbade it entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Wan and Xiang are fertile; early in the dynasty settlers opened fields as hereditary holdings and suits were barred for a century—litigious men now used tenant-exchange laws to disrupt this, and You forbade it entirely.

sentences.zh: 有持獻於權貴而降中旨給賜者，卣言：「地盈千頃，戶且數百，傳子至孫久，一旦改隸，眾將不安。

translations.literal: Some presented land to powerful figures and received secret edicts of grant; You said, "The land spans a thousand qing and hundreds of households have held it from fathers to grandsons—suddenly to change jurisdiction will unsettle the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: When powerful men received secret grants of presented land, You said, "These estates span a thousand qing and hundreds of households have held them for generations—sudden transfer will unsettle everyone.

sentences.zh: 先朝明詔具在，不可易也。」

translations.literal: The former court's clear edicts remain in force and cannot be altered."
translations.idiomatic: The former court's clear edicts still stand and cannot be changed."

sentences.zh: 朝廷是其議。

translations.literal: The court approved his argument.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 提點湖南刑獄，知鼎、遼、隴、寧四州，復提舉潼川路刑獄。

translations.literal: He was put in charge of criminal cases in Hunan, governed the four prefectures of Ding, Liao, Long, and Ning, and again oversaw criminal cases on the Tongchuan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw Hunan criminal justice, governed Ding, Liao, Long, and Ning, and again supervised Tongchuan circuit criminal affairs.

sentences.zh: 有議榷酤於瀘、敘間，雲歲可得錢二十萬。

translations.literal: Some proposed state monopoly wine sales between Lu and Xu, saying two hundred thousand strings could be gained yearly.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed a wine monopoly between Lu and Xu, promising two hundred thousand strings a year.

sentences.zh: 卣言：「先朝念此地夷漢雜居，故弛其榷禁，以惠安邊人。

translations.literal: You said, "The former court, mindful that this region mixes Yi and Han, relaxed the monopoly to benefit and pacify the frontier people.
translations.idiomatic: You said, "The former court relaxed the monopoly here because Yi and Han live mixed together, to benefit frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 今之所行，未見其利。」

translations.literal: What is now proposed shows no clear benefit."
translations.idiomatic: The proposed change shows no clear benefit."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: It was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: It was dropped.

sentences.zh: 累官中大夫，卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: He rose to Grandee of Palace Attendance and died at the age of seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Grandee of Palace Attendance and died at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 論曰：「何㮚、孫傅、聶昌皆疏俊之士，而器質窳薄，使當重任於艱難之秋，宋事蓋可知矣，欽宗之再詣金營，㮚實誤之，一死不足償也。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: "He Li, Sun Fu, and Nie Chang were all open and talented men, yet their substance was shallow; to place them in heavy responsibility in a time of hardship—the outcome for Song can be imagined. Qinzong's second journey to the Jin camp was truly misled by Li; one death cannot repay it.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: "He Li, Sun Fu, and Nie Chang were talented but shallow men; giving them grave duties in crisis foretold Song's fate. Li truly misled Qinzong's second visit to the Jin camp—his death could not atone for it.

sentences.zh: 傅匿太子之謀甚疏，昌河東之行尤謬，效死弗當，徒傷勇爾。

translations.literal: Fu's plot to hide the crown prince was very crude; Chang's journey to Hedong was especially absurd—they died without deserving it and merely wasted their courage.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's plot to hide the crown prince was crude; Chang's Hedong mission was absurd—their deaths were misapplied courage.

sentences.zh: 過庭因方臘之亂，乞誅蔡京、王黼、朱勔以謝天下，庶幾有敢諫之風焉。

translations.literal: Guoting, on the Fang La rebellion, asked to execute Cai Jing, Wang Fu, and Zhu Xun to answer the realm—there was perhaps something of the spirit of daring remonstrance in this.
translations.idiomatic: Guoting, amid the Fang La rebellion, demanded the execution of Cai Jing, Wang Fu, and Zhu Xun to satisfy the realm—here at least was the spirit of bold remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「尺有所不逮，寸有所不覃。」

translations.literal: The Classic of History says, "The foot-rule has what it cannot reach; the inch has what it cannot cover."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says, "Even a foot-rule cannot measure everything; even an inch cannot cover all."

sentences.zh: 觀二張之理郡，鄭僅之守藩，宇文父子之便邊糶、革馬政，許幾、程之邵之經制財運，蒲卣之議稅榷，皆有可稱道。

translations.literal: Observing the two Zhangs' governance of prefectures, Zheng Jin's defense of a circuit, the Yuwen father and son's easing of frontier grain sales and reform of horse policy, Xu Ji and Cheng Zhi Shao's management of finance and transport, and Pu You's arguments on taxes and monopolies—all have points worth praise.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the two Zhangs' prefectural rule, Zheng Jin's frontier defense, the Yuwen men's grain and horse reforms, Xu Ji and Cheng Zhi Shao's fiscal management, and Pu You's tax and monopoly policies—all deserve praise.

sentences.zh: 若閣之固寵于花石，而龔原、崔公度主王氏學以諂事安石，則搢紳所不齒也。」

translations.literal: As for Ge's clinging to favor through the Flower and Stone Bureau, and Gong Yuan and Cui Gongdu's leadership of Wang's learning to flatter and serve Anshi—these the gentry do not regard as their peers."
translations.idiomatic: But Ge's clinging to favor through the Flower and Stone Bureau, and Gong Yuan and Cui Gongdu's promotion of Wang's learning to flatter Anshi—these men the gentry will not acknowledge."
